How it was found: the committed lockfile, `npm ci`, then the `package.json` edit and ONE `npm install` (card 68), which
moved only the Sanity subtree (`added 73, removed 151, changed 180`). `npm install` prints `ERESOLVE overriding peer
dependency`: that is `@sanity/astro`'s `^5.5.0` peer meeting the visual-editing override, and it is expected.

**Invariants, measured.** `find node_modules -path "*@sanity/ui/package.json"`: one line (4.4.9).
`find node_modules -path "*@sanity/icons/package.json"`: one line (5.2.3). `grep -l "errors.md#" dist/client/_astro/*.js`:
one file. Four `@sanity/client` 7.27.0 copies stay nested, under `@sanity/presentation-comlink` (types only; its dist never
imports the client) and three `@sanity/workflow-*` CLI packages. Those are upstream's own ranges and the client is
stateless, so leave them.

**Migration notes, per change.** Most of it is mechanical and `astro check` finds it, with two exceptions marked.

1. **`space` is gone; use `gap`.** `Stack`, `Inline`, `Select`, `Hotkeys` and friends type `space?: never`. 47 uses across
   `checkPage`, `saveSectionPreset`, `BrandKit`, `BusinessOverview`, `CharacterCountInput`, `GuideView`, `PreviewNavigator`,
   `SeoSnippetInput` and `StudioGuide`. `sed -i 's/\bspace={/gap={/g'` on the files `astro check` names. The error reads
   `Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'undefined'`, which does not say "renamed".
2. **`Grid columns` is `gridTemplateColumns`** (and `rows`, `column`, `columnStart` and the rest become `grid*`). One use,
   `BrandKit`.
3. **`Badge mode` is gone** ("No longer used"). One use, `CharacterCountInput` (`mode="outline"` dropped; the tone still
   colours it).
4. **Subpath-only components.** `Menu`, `MenuButton`, `MenuItem`, `MenuDivider`, `MenuGroup` come from `@sanity/ui/menu`;
   `useToast`, `Toast`, `ToastProvider` from `@sanity/ui/toast`; also `/tooltip`, `/popover`, `/autocomplete`,
   `/breadcrumbs`, `/code`. The root still declares them, as `never`, so the error is `This expression is not callable` or
   `JSX element type 'MenuItem' does not have any construct or call signatures`. Eight files (`useToast` in seven, `Menu*`
   in `PreviewNavigator`).
5. **`@sanity/icons` 5 has no named root exports (NOT caught by `astro check`).** The root exports only `Icon` and `icons`;
   every icon is `import { BellIcon } from '@sanity/icons/Bell'`. The root declares the old names as `never`, and a `never`
   passed to `icon:` type-checks, so `astro check` is clean and `astro build` then fails with
   `[MISSING_EXPORT] "BellIcon" is not exported by "node_modules/@sanity/icons/dist/index.js"`. 16 files, about 70 imports,
   rewritten as one import line per icon. **A `// scaffold: x` comment on a name's line must move onto that icon's new
   line** (`structure.ts` carries one on `OlistIcon`), or `npm run scaffold -- --remove` stops removing it (rule 14).
6. **The dev Studio needs `react/compiler-runtime` pre-bundled (NOT caught by the build or CI).** `astro.config.mjs` excludes
   `@sanity/ui` from `optimizeDeps` (a v3-era workaround, kept). `@sanity/ui` 4 is React Compiler output and imports React's
   CommonJS `react/compiler-runtime`; an excluded package's imports are served raw, so `astro dev` serves a blank `/studio`
   with `[astro-island] Error hydrating ... studio-component.tsx SyntaxError: The requested module
'/node_modules/react/compiler-runtime.js' does not provide an export named 'c'`. @sanity/astro's own include list names
   the older `react-compiler-runtime` package, not this one. Fix: `optimizeDeps.include: ['react/compiler-runtime']`.
   `astro build` never hits it. Same symptom as card 60's rejected alternative, different cause.
7. **`@sanity/ui/styles.css` is imported by `sanity` itself** (`sanity/lib/index.js`), so an embedded Studio needs no import
   of its own. It lands as one more `<link rel="stylesheet">` on `/studio`, which is the only parity diff (12/12 after
   recapturing `studio` alone; every content page byte-identical).
8. **The module docs' code snippets** (`docs/modules/*.md`, `archive/modules/*/*.md`) carried the old icon imports and are
   rewritten the same way, so installing a module does not bring the root import back.

Unchanged and verified: `buildTheme({ font })` from `@sanity/ui/theme` (light and dark), `useClient`,
`usePresentationNavigate` / `usePresentationParams`, `createPreviewSecret`, `validatePreviewUrl`, `perspectiveCookieName`,
every `@sanity/visual-editing` subpath the overlay uses (`/react`, `/optimistic`, `/create-data-attribute`), and
`fixSanityDedupeAlias()` (card 60; @sanity/astro 3.5.1 still has the forward-slash regex).

**Gates (starter, 2026-10-17, Windows 11, Node 24.16.0).** `npm run typegen` passes; `astro check` 0 errors; lint 0 errors
(the 7 known warnings); `test:unit` 638 + 54 pass; `npm run build` passes; `npm test` 120/120; `npm run parity compare`
12/12 after the studio recapture. `npm audit`: 42 (`origin/main`'s lockfile the same day: 44; phase 2 drops
`@module-federation/*`, `@sanity/workbench-cli` and `adm-zip`, and adds the CLI-only `@sanity/cli-build` and
`@sanity/runtime-cli`).

**Browser verification.** The starter has no Sanity project, so the worktree was pointed at first-baptist-auburn's
pre-launch project through an uncommitted `.env` and `.dev.vars` and opened in a signed-in Chrome. On `astro dev`: the desk,
Help & Guide (GuideView), Start Here (StudioGuide, BusinessOverview, BrandKit with its two-column grid), a page document
(CharacterCountInput badge, SeoSnippetInput, the custom document actions menu, the Check this page dialog) and Media, all
with a clean console. On the BUILT site under `wrangler dev`: Presentation (`/studio/#/presentation`) with PreviewNavigator,
the preview iframe on `/preview/`, `GET /preview/live/ 200` (the SSE proxy), stega present in the iframe text, and the
overlay box drawing on hover; light and dark appearance both correct. **Not exercised:** an in-canvas control writing back,
which would leave a draft in a client dataset. Each site's PR repeats the check against its own project.

**Rolling it to a site.** One PR per site, in this order: first-baptist-auburn (pre-launch), presacademy, reid-design-site,
mas-monograms, stonesteps-50k, fbcm. Seven of the changed files are `PORTABLE` (`checkPage`, `saveSectionPreset`,
`SeoSnippetInput`, `UndoRedo`, `pageActions`, `shareDraftLink`, `slugRedirect`), so the marked-file order applies: the
starter merges first, then each site PR carries the new copies and is green on its first run. Until a site's PR lands,
sync-check reports DRIFT for those seven files on that site, which is expected. In each site:

1. `npm ci`, then set the exact versions above in `package.json` (both `@sanity/visual-editing` entries, and the
   `sanity-plugin-utils` override to 2.0.22), then ONE `npm install`. Keep the site's other overrides. Check the disk
   invariants.
2. Copy the seven PORTABLE files from the starter and add `'react/compiler-runtime'` to `optimizeDeps.include`.
3. Run `astro check` and fix items 1 to 4 in the site's OWN Studio files (most sites have 20 to 30 files importing
   `@sanity/ui` or `@sanity/icons`; mas-monograms has 52).
4. Rewrite the icon imports (item 5) in `src` AND in root files (`sanity.config.ts`, `sanity.cli.ts`: mas-monograms
   imports `ActivityIcon` in its root config, which a `src`-only codemod missed and only the build caught), then
   `grep -rn "from '@sanity/icons'" src *.ts` must print nothing but `Icon` / `icons`.
   Then `npm run build`, because only the build catches a missed icon.
5. `typegen`, `check`, `build:full`, `test:unit`, `npm test`, `parity compare` (expect only `studio` to move).
6. `astro dev`, open `/studio` signed in, read the console, open every custom pane and action; then the built site under
   `npm run preview` for Presentation.

**Learned on the site branches (2026-10-17).**

- **vite moves with it.** `@sanity/cli-build` (under `sanity` 6.19) requires `vite ^8.3.3`, so a site still on vite 8.2.x
  gets 8.3.4 (and rolldown 1.2.14) from the one `npm install`. stonesteps-50k did; the starter and first-baptist-auburn were
  already there. Expected, not lockfile drift. Other non-Sanity movement in that install is Sanity's own subtree (Sentry,
  Mux, groq, i18next).
- **`grep -l "errors.md#"` can list two files.** reid-design-site and mas-monograms bundle `polished` (a `sanity`
  dependency) into its own chunk, and polished links its own `errors.md`. Grep the styled-components path instead:
  `grep -lF 'packages/styled-components/src/utils/errors.md#' dist/client/_astro/*.js` must list ONE file.
- **The Presentation enable URL needs its slash** on a site with `trailingSlash: 'always'` (card 89):
  `previewMode: { enable: '/api/draft-mode/enable/' }`. presacademy, reid-design-site and fbcm still had the slash-less
  path, which answers a 301 before the real 302 into `/preview/`. Fixed in their phase-2 PRs.
- **Testing Presentation locally on a site with `upgrade-insecure-requests` in its CSP** (presacademy's `_headers`):
  under `wrangler dev` on plain http, the iframe's redirect into `/preview/` is upgraded to `https://localhost`, fails,
  and Presentation says "Unable to connect to visual editing". Production is https and unaffected. For a local check only,
  delete `; upgrade-insecure-requests` from the BUILT `dist/client/_headers` (never from `public/_headers`).
- **Embedded-Studio hash routes.** Deep links are `/studio/#/presentation`, not `/studio/presentation` (a 404 on the
  built site). And a hash-only navigation does not reload the page, so after swapping `astro dev` for `wrangler dev` on the
  same port, reload before reading the console, or the old dev page's errors show up.

**Status, 2026-10-17.** Starter: `yes` (#128). Every site merged the same day, one PR each, each Studio and
Presentation checked signed in: first-baptist-auburn (fbc-auburn#15, no matrix column), presacademy (#103),
reid-design-site (#153), mas-monograms (#114), stonesteps-50k (#123), fbcm (#68, no matrix column). 2ndpreschicago is
archived and stays on the phase-1 set (`no`).

## Card 104: a reskinned fork keeps working: default fields, default hrefs, layout gate, OG theme (2026-10-17)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's first reskin (fbc-auburn PR #17, branch `reskin/auburn-mockups`), the first fork to
change its layout slots and brand colours with `apply-brand` and then run every gate. Four starter bugs, each one that
every later fork would hit. A fifth turned up while writing the guard test.
**Canonical:** `src/data/defaultSections.ts`, `src/components/CtaLink.astro`, `src/lib/site-layout.test.ts`,
`src/lib/default-sections.test.ts` (new), `scripts/apply-brand.mjs`, `scripts/og-theme.mjs` (new),
`scripts/generate-og-default.mjs`, `scripts/generate-og-pages.mjs`. None is PORTABLE, so no site turns red; each site
copies the change by hand.

1. **Default section headings never rendered.** The `richTextSection` and `imageTextSection` defaults named their
   heading `headline`; the schema and both components use `heading`. The home richText default also carried a `cta`
   the block has no field for, and the process spacer a `size` (the field is `variant`). Fixed in the data, and
   `default-sections.test.ts` now reads both files as text and fails on any default field the block's schema lacks
   (a text parse because `defaultSections.ts` imports through the `@/` alias, which plain node cannot resolve).
   `npm run seed` writes these arrays, so a seeded project got the wrong field too.
2. **Every default button went to `/contact/`.** `resolveHref` in `CtaLink.astro` returned `fallbackHref` whenever a
   CTA had no `linkType`, and the built-in defaults never have one: they name an `href`. Now
   `if (!c?.linkType) return c?.href ?? fallbackHref;`, with `href?: string` on the type. Two default hrefs that had
   been hidden by the bug were then wrong: the home hero's `/portfolio/` (no such route; now "About the Studio",
   `/about/`) and the home services button's `/services/` (now carries `// scaffold: services` so a fork without
   services loses the button instead of a 404; the hero button carries `// scaffold: about`).
3. **The layout gate failed any fork that picks a layout.** `site-layout.test.ts` asserted
   `brand.config.json` layout equalled `DEFAULT_LAYOUT`, so choosing a hero or header variant (the point of card 72's
   slots) failed `test:unit`. It now checks the config names only real values (`resolveLayout(config.layout)` returns
   it unchanged) and that `src/data/layout.ts` carries each value, i.e. apply-brand was run after the config changed.
4. **apply-brand made every reskinned fork DRIFT.** It rewrote the `DEFAULTS` in `scripts/lib/render-og.mjs`, which
   is PORTABLE, so `sync-check` reported DRIFT the moment a fork took its own colours. The brand now goes in
   `scripts/og-theme.mjs` (`OG_THEME`, safe to edit, fork-owned), which both OG generators pass as renderOg's existing
   `theme` option; apply-brand rewrites `og-theme.mjs` by the same regexes and never touches `render-og.mjs`.
   render-og's header comment, which still said apply-brand rewrites its DEFAULTS, was corrected in the follow-up below.

**Adopting it in a site.** Copy the four test/data/component changes where the site still has the starter's form (grep
for `if (!c?.linkType) return fallbackHref`, `ships the defaults`, `headline` inside richText/imageText defaults).
For the OG half: add `scripts/og-theme.mjs` with the site's CURRENT colours (read them from its `render-og.mjs`
DEFAULTS), import it in both generators as `theme: OG_THEME`, copy `rewriteOgTheme` into `apply-brand.mjs`, then
restore `render-og.mjs` to the starter's copy and confirm `npm run sync-check` and `npm run og` (the image must not
change). A site with a hand-written `defaultSections.ts` runs `default-sections.test.ts` first; it may find more.

**Verified (starter).** `default-sections.test.ts` fails on `origin/main`'s `defaultSections.ts` (richText
`headline`, spacer `size`) and passes after; `npm run apply-brand -- --check` matches every pattern in
`og-theme.mjs` with "no changes" (the theme file holds the starter's own values); gates as listed in the changelog.

**Status, 2026-10-17.** Starter `yes`. first-baptist-auburn carries 1 to 3 and `scripts/og-theme.mjs` (fbc-auburn #17;
the starter's file has the same shape). The rest (`rewriteOgTheme` in its `apply-brand.mjs`, the
`default-sections` test, the spacer and its own leftover `headline` defaults) goes in its resync PR after the follow-up below.

**Follow-up, 2026-10-17 (same day).** `defaultSections.ts` had carried mis-encoded characters since before the
scaffold work: UTF-8 em-dashes read once as Windows-1252, so two default sentences rendered `â€”` on the page (and
would have been em-dashes in site copy anyway, rule 2). The copy now uses a comma and a colon, the comments' box-drawing
rules are repaired, and `default-sections.test.ts` fails on an em-dash or a stray `â` outside a comment. The stale
`render-og.mjs` header comment now says the brand goes in through `theme` from `scripts/og-theme.mjs`. That file is
PORTABLE, and of the matrix sites only first-baptist-auburn marks it, so fbc-auburn is the one site resync (its PR also
takes `rewriteOgTheme`, the test and the spacer fix).

## Card 105: a text hero still renders its buttons (2026-10-17)

**Origin:** found while verifying card 104 in the starter. `Hero.astro` has two branches: the photo hero (CTAs over the
image) and the text hero, used when there is no image or the `editorial` hero variant is chosen. The text branch rendered
only `SectionHeading`, so its `primaryCta` and `secondaryCta` were silently dropped. A home page without a hero photo,
which is every fresh fork and every unseeded build, had no buttons above the fold, and a site that picks the editorial hero
lost them for good.
**Canonical:** `src/components/Hero.astro` (not PORTABLE).

**The fix.** The text branch wraps `SectionHeading` and, when the block has CTAs, the same `mt-l flex flex-wrap gap-s` button
row the photo hero uses, without `onDark` (the text hero sits on `bg-background`). Interior pages whose hero carries no CTAs
render exactly as before.

**Adopting it in a site.** Only where the site still has the starter's text branch (grep `Hero.astro` for a
`SectionHeading ... level="h1"` with no `CtaLink` after it). Check light and dark at 375 and 1280 on a page whose text hero
has buttons, and regenerate visual baselines if the home hero has no photo.

**Status, 2026-10-17.** Starter `yes`.

## Card 106: the Studio kit: Home, Site Guide, Checkup, staff view, Trash (2026-10-17)

**Origin:** the family's WordPress sites give staff a plain admin (a Home page, a printable guide, a fix-it list, a
staff menu with no permanent deletes, a safer trash). The Sanity sites had pieces of it scattered across client repos
(mas-monograms' Checkup, Trash and publish note; presacademy's tour) and nothing shared. first-baptist-auburn built the
kit first (fbc-auburn#23), with every generic file free of site names and one site file, so it could come back here
unchanged.
**Canonical:** PORTABLE: `src/sanity/kit/` (`index.tsx`, `types.ts`, `shared.tsx`, `HomeTool.tsx`, `GuideTool.tsx`,
`CheckupTool.tsx`, `StudioTour.tsx`, `trash.tsx`, `publishNote.tsx`), `src/lib/studio-kit.ts`,
`src/lib/studio-checkup.ts`, `src/lib/studio-trash.ts` and their three `.test.ts` files, `src/pages/build-info.json.ts`,
`docs/agent/studio-kit.md`. Per site (NOT portable): `src/sanity/kit.config.ts`, the `structure.ts` desk changes, the
`astro.config.mjs` define, and the plugin line in `sanity.config.ts`.

**What it adds.** `ncsStudioKit(kitConfig)`, LAST in `plugins`: Home (first tool, so the Studio opens on it: welcome,
This week, Is it live?, Site health, Recent edits, Visitors placeholder, Ask), Site Guide (the existing guides, searched
and printable), Checkup (pure rules over one fetch, unit-tested), plain tool names ("Content", "Live preview"), the
staff view (listed Sanity user ids, or non-administrators when the list is empty: fewer tools, no Delete, no perspective
menu or Releases link), Move to Trash with a `trashedItem` type and "Bring it back", a note after Publish, and a
first-run tour. Detail: `docs/agent/studio-kit.md`.

**Desk changes in `structure.ts`** (take them with the kit): singleton items get `.id(schemaType)` (an intent link from
Home or the Checkup resolves to `pages;aboutPage`, and a title-derived id opened a blank pane); `.id('start-here')` and
`.id('content')` so `staffHiddenPanes` can name them; a Trash list item with id `trash` (the Checkup links to it); the
safety net filters every `media.*` type (sanity-plugin-media 6 added `media.folder`, which leaked a "Media Folder" list
into the desk root); and the desk is wrapped as `staffDesk(fullDesk(S, context), context, kitConfig)`.

**The bug fixed on the way.** `/build-info.json` read `process.env.GITHUB_SHA` in the route. The route prerenders inside
workerd, which cannot see the build machine's environment, so Auburn's deployed file always said `"commit": null`.
`astro.config.mjs` now reads the SHA in Node (`GITHUB_SHA`, then `git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD`, else null) and hands it
to the route as the Vite define `__NCS_BUILD_COMMIT__`. Verified with a local `npm run build`: `dist/client/build-info.json`
carried the short HEAD SHA.

**Starter defaults.** `kit.config.ts` is neutral: `staff: []`, `thisWeek: []`, `genericRules()` with the starter's SEO page
types, trash types for the everyday lists, tour words with no site in them, helper "your web designer". Entries tied to
a capability carry scaffold markers, so `npm run scaffold -- --remove` keeps the file compiling; the PORTABLE kit files
carry none (card 99).

**Adopting it in a site.** Copy the PORTABLE files, write `kit.config.ts` from the starter's, take the four

`@sanity/ui` 4 only (card 103).

**Status, 2026-10-17.** Starter `yes`. first-baptist-auburn (no matrix column) is the origin and swaps its copies for the
marked ones in the PR that follows this card. Every other site `no`; the Worker half (visitors, Ask form, deploy status,
monthly report) is `docs/PENDING.md` item 14.

## Card 107: hidden reveal states wait for `html.motion`, so no-JS shows the finished page (2026-10-17)

**Origin:** found on first-baptist-auburn while checking reported "blank sections" on the home page. The blanks were only
the 600ms reveal fade, but the check showed that `globals.css` set `[data-reveal] { opacity: 0 }` (and the same for
`[data-stagger-grid] > *` and a covering `.img-curtain`) unconditionally, and only BaseLayout's IntersectionObserver
ever adds the class that shows them. With JavaScript off, blocked or failed to load, most sections of every page stayed
invisible for good. Only reduced-motion visitors were safe, because the reduced-motion block forces the end state.
**Canonical:** `src/styles/globals.css` and `src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro` (both foundation files, not PORTABLE).

**The fix.** The inline theme bootstrap in BaseLayout's `<head>` now also toggles `motion` on `<html>` (on unless the
visitor prefers reduced motion). It runs before first paint and again on `astro:after-swap`, because the view-transition
swap resets `<html>`'s className. In `globals.css` every hidden START state moved under that class:
`html.motion [data-reveal]`, `html.motion [data-stagger-grid] > *` and `html.motion .img-curtain` (the curtain now
defaults to `scaleY(0)`, open). The matching end states took the same prefix
(`html.motion [data-reveal].is-visible`, `html.motion [data-stagger-grid].is-staggered > *`,
`html.motion .img-curtain.is-revealed`) so they still outrank the start states. The transition declarations stay on the
unprefixed selectors, so nothing that overrides their timing (`[data-stagger-grid] > .card-lift-slow`,
`.is-filtered-out`) changes specificity. With JS on, the picture and timing are unchanged; with JS off the page renders
finished. Any new hidden-until-JS state goes under `html.motion` too. Not covered: a page whose inline head script runs but
whose bundled module fails, which still waits on the observer.

**Adopting it in a site.** Where `globals.css` still has `[data-reveal] {` with `opacity: 0` at top level (grep it with
one line of context): copy the three CSS blocks and the head-script toggle. A site that already sets a class like this
(`js`, `motion`, `reveal-ready`) can scope to that class instead of adding a second. Verify in a real browser with
JavaScript disabled (Playwright `javaScriptEnabled: false`: no element under `[data-reveal]`, `[data-stagger-grid]` or
`.img-curtain` should compute to opacity 0 or cover the image), then with JS on, scrolling a long page, to check the fade
still plays. Visual baselines should not move, since the Playwright settle helper adds the end classes anyway.

**Status, 2026-10-17.** Starter `yes`. mas-monograms and nixoncreativestudio `partial` (already gated on their own head
class). presacademy, reid-design-site and stonesteps-50k `yes` (2026-10-17). first-baptist-auburn (no column) already sets
`html.motion` for its own `motion.css` and scopes its `globals.css` copies in the PR that follows this card. fbcm (no column)
took it too (fbcm#70).

**Watch for site variants when adopting.** `html.motion [data-reveal]` is (0,2,1), so a site rule such as
`[data-reveal='arch'] { opacity: 1 }` or `[data-reveal].reveal-l { translate: -1.5rem 0 }` now LOSES to the base start
state: with JS on the figure fades as a whole box, or the directional slide becomes a plain rise. Prefix those variants
with `html.motion` too (fbcm did its whole arch/mark/draw/ink/sign block, presacademy its `.reveal-l`/`.reveal-r`,
`.reveal-rise` and eyebrow rules). Descendant start states that hide content (`[data-reveal] .wx__bar { scaleY(0) }`, a
clipped `.reveal-rise` headline) take it as well, start AND end, or the prefixed start outranks the old end. In an Astro
scoped `<style>`, write `:global(html.motion) .x[data-reveal] ...`.

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** The rollout report does not name this card per site. All five sites are synced to starter a837dc3 (synced, not individually verified).

## Card 108: the header logo renders with JavaScript off (2026-10-17)

**Origin:** found on first-baptist-auburn while verifying card 107 with JavaScript off. Every section showed, but the
header logo was only its alt text. The theme-aware header `<img data-theme-logo>` ships with no `src` or `srcset` on
purpose, so the browser fetches nothing until the inline script after it picks the light or dark variant from
`html.dark`. That keeps one logo fetch per page load, and it also means no JS, no logo.
**Canonical:** `src/components/Header.astro` (foundation, not PORTABLE).

**The fix.** Right after the swap img, and only when no Site Settings logo is uploaded, the header renders a
`<noscript>` copy of the logo with the light variant's `src` (a no-JS visitor never gets `html.dark`, so light is the
right one). A scoped rule in the header's `<style>`, `img[data-theme-logo]:not([src]) { display: none; }`, hides the
src-less swap img, which only stays src-less when the inline script never ran. With JS on, `<noscript>` content is not
parsed as markup, so nothing extra is fetched and the single-fetch behaviour is unchanged. The footer logo already
carries the light `src` (it is lazy, so the swap lands before it loads) and needs nothing. The uploaded-logo branch
always had a `src`.

**Adopting it in a site.** Where `Header.astro` has an `img` with `data-theme-logo` and no `src` attribute: copy the
`<noscript>` block (match the swap img's width, height and class) and the scoped CSS rule. Verify with Playwright
`javaScriptEnabled: false`: the visible header logo has `naturalWidth > 0` and the src-less img computes to
`display: none`. Then with JS on, in light and dark: one logo request per load and the right variant shown.

**Status, 2026-10-17.** Starter `yes`. stonesteps-50k had the same src-less header logo and took it the same day
(stonesteps-50k#126), hence `yes`. The other matrix sites have no theme-aware header logo (`n/a`). first-baptist-auburn
(no column) took it in fbc-auburn#31.

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** The rollout report does not name this card per site. All five sites are synced to starter a837dc3 (synced, not individually verified).

## Card 109: the authoring kit: page templates, a picture picker, patterns, synced sections, guardrails (2026-10-18)

**Origin:** the starter, so a client can build pages themselves the way a WordPress block-editor handover allows. The
page builder already had the blocks, the grouped insert menu (card 17) and saved sections (card 24); what was missing
was a start that is not an empty page, a way to choose a block by how it looks, a way to reuse a GROUP of blocks, a
block that stays the same everywhere, and a word of warning before an easy mistake goes live.
**Canonical:** the starter. No file in it is marked PORTABLE: templates and rules are per site by design, and the rest
touches foundation files each site has adapted (`sections.ts`, `queries.ts`, `SectionRenderer.astro`).

**What it is.**

- **Page templates.** `src/sanity/pageTemplates.ts` (the site's own list) becomes initial value templates on `page` in
  `sanity.config.ts`; `value` is a function so each new page gets fresh `_key`s (`freshKeys()`); `newDocumentOptions`
  hides the stock `page` template behind "Blank page". Example text starts `Example:`.
- **Picture picker.** `SECTION_INSERT_MENU.views` is `[grid, list]`; `previewImageUrl` points at
  `/section-thumbnails/<type>.jpg`, shot by `npm run thumbnails` from `/styleguide/sections/` (every block, fixed data,
  the real `SectionRenderer`), so the pictures carry the site's brand. Missing picture: Sanity falls back to the icon.
- **Patterns.** `sectionPreset.section` holds up to 12 sections (was max 1; old presets stay valid). Every
  `pageBuilder` spreads `pageBuilderAuthoring`, whose input adds "Insert a saved section": Add a copy (deep, fresh keys)
  or Add synced (published presets only). The navigator's Saved sections panel adds a whole pattern in order.
- **Synced sections.** `syncedSection` references a preset; `sectionsProjection()` resolves it through the shared
  `SECTION_ARMS`; `SectionRenderer` expands it before the cadence (`expandSyncedSections()`), so rule 9 holds and the
  section-fields gate scans it. `_editKey` points in-canvas controls at the synced block. A preset's member list
  (`LIBRARY_SECTION_TYPES`) excludes `syncedSection`, so no loop can exist.
- **Guardrails.** Validation WARNINGS only, never errors, so nothing valid before can be blocked from Publish: empty
  section, leftover `Example:` text, synced section with nothing picked, plus `pageRules` in `kit.config.ts`
  (`appliesTo`, `mustStartWith`, `atMostOnce`, `maxSections`).
- Three Site Guide guides; detail in `docs/agent/sanity.md`.

**Tests.** `src/lib/authoring.test.ts` (keys, patterns, expansion, example marker, every template, and "every block has
a fixture on the wall and a thumbnail on disk") and `src/lib/page-guardrails.test.ts`.

**Adopting it in a site.** Copy `src/lib/authoring.ts`, `src/lib/page-guardrails.ts` and their tests,
`src/sanity/pageBuilderAuthoring.ts`, `components/PageBuilderInput.tsx`, `scripts/shoot-section-thumbnails.mjs` and the
`thumbnails` npm script. Write the site's own `pageTemplates.ts` (only block types its custom page accepts) and
`pageRules`. Hand-merge: the `syncedSection` type, `LIBRARY_SECTION_TYPES` and the grid view in `sections.ts`; the
preset changes; `SECTION_ARMS` in `queries.ts`; the expansion and `editKeyOf` in `SectionRenderer.astro`; the spread
into each `pageBuilder`; `syncedSection` in `SELF_FILLING_SECTIONS`; the navigator's pattern loop; the templates in
`sanity.config.ts`. Build `/styleguide/sections/` from the site's own blocks, `npm run build`, `npm run thumbnails`,
commit the pictures. Then `npm run typegen` (new `syncedSection` type) and open `/studio` logged in: make a page from
each template, open "+ Add item" in grid view, insert a pattern as a copy and as synced, and read the console.

**Status, 2026-10-18.** Starter `yes` (draft PR). Every site `no`; 2ndpreschicago and ncs-church-starter `n/a`
(archived), wcp `n/a` (retired). Not yet verified logged in to a Studio: the picker grid, the insert dialog and the
template menu were type-checked and built, not clicked.

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** Applied on presacademy, reid-design-site, mas-monograms, stonesteps-50k. On the other sites it is synced to starter a837dc3 only (synced, not individually verified).

**Correction, 2026-10-26 (card 173).** Re-checked on each `origin/main`. mas-monograms has only `src/lib/authoring.ts` (its `EXAMPLE_PREFIX` feeds `studio-prepublish.ts`): no page templates, no grid view or thumbnails, no `syncedSection` type. Its cell moves from `yes` to `partial`. presacademy keeps `yes`: the kit is there under its own names (templates in `src/sanity/templates.ts` with "Group: Title" menu names, the insert menu with `views` and `previewImageUrl` inline in `schemaTypes/blocks.ts`, thumbnails in `public/studio-thumbs/`, `syncedSection` in `blocks.ts` and resolved in `queries.ts`), so an audit that greps for `pageTemplates.ts` or `SECTION_INSERT_MENU` misses it.

## Card 110: the Studio looks like the site: name, mark, colours, status line, help panel, Home round two (2026-10-18)

**Origin:** the Studio research of 2026-10-18 (plan items 1, 2, 7, 9, 10 and 12). Two findings started it. Every fork
registered a `StudioLogo` wordmark as `studio.components.logo`, which Sanity 6 marks deprecated and never draws: checked
in a dev server, the login screen showed Sanity's generated "MS" chip and "My Studio", and the tab showed Sanity's logo.
And the Studio's colours were stock Sanity blue and grey on every client, so it read as someone else's software.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE: `src/sanity/components/StudioIdentity.tsx`, `src/sanity/studioTheme.ts`,
`src/lib/studio-theme.ts` and `studio-theme.test.ts`, `src/sanity/kit/NavbarStatus.tsx`, `src/sanity/kit/HelpPanel.tsx`,
and the card-110 changes to `kit/HomeTool.tsx`, `kit/shared.tsx`, `kit/index.tsx`, `kit/types.ts`, `kit/publishNote.tsx`,
`src/lib/studio-kit.ts` (+ test), `src/sanity/actions/checkPage.tsx` (`runPageCheck`) and `docs/agent/studio-kit.md`.
Per site (NOT portable): the `sanity.config.ts` lines (title, icon, `applySiteFavicon`, `...studioThemeColors`),
`kit.config.ts` (`quickActions`, `guide.forType`, `pageCheck`, `features.navbarStatus`, `features.helpPanel`),
`resolve.ts` (the every-page locations), the two guides and `GUIDES_FOR_TYPE` appended to `guides/content.ts`, and the
`apply-brand.mjs` / schema check. `StudioLogo.tsx` is deleted.

**What it adds.**

- **Name and mark.** Workspace `title` is `brand.config.json` `name`; workspace `icon` draws `public/favicon.svg` (the one
  drawing the whole icon set comes from, already legible at 16px with its own dark colours); the same file replaces
  Sanity's logo in the Studio tab, and the login tab is titled with the site name. `apply-brand` prints the title and
  warns when the brand name has changed but `favicon.svg` is still the starter's "S".
- **Colours, without a new dependency.** `@sanity/themer` wants React `^19.3.0`, outside the matched set (rule 8), so
  the theme stays on `@sanity/ui`'s own `buildTheme({ palette, color })`: the accent (`studio.accent`, else
  `palette.light --primary`) replaces Sanity's blue scale (primary buttons, links, focus rings, the selected row), the
  site's light and dark `--background` replace palette white and black, and one token makes the dark page background
  palette black. Green, amber, red and purple are Sanity's own on every client. `@sanity/color` (the default palette) is
  imported as the transitive dependency both `sanity` and `@sanity/ui` pin, so package.json does not change.
- **The contrast guard.** The brand gives the scale its hue and saturation only; each step's lightness is solved to match
  the luminance of Sanity's tuned blue step, then 500 (light buttons) and 400 (dark buttons) are pushed to 4.5:1 (stock
  Sanity's own 500 is 4.29:1). A background that is not light (or dark) enough, or any non-hex value, falls back to
  Sanity's with a note. `studio-theme.test.ts` runs the real `buildTheme` for this site's brand and three awkward ones
  (pale gold, near-white sage, pastel pink) and asserts button labels and links at 4.5:1, focus rings at 3:1, the
  backgrounds, and unchanged status hues, in both schemes. A reskin that breaks it fails `test:unit`.
- **Status line** under the top bar ("Website up to date" / "Updating the website, about 3 minutes" / caution after
  `liveSlowAfterMinutes`), a navbar middleware that always calls `renderDefault`, sharing `useLiveData()` with Home.
- **Help for this page**, a document inspector: the page check and the Checkup findings for the document, then its Site
  Guide entries by type.
- **Home round two**: a greeting and the site's name in the display font on a `tone="primary"` card; quick actions from
  `kitConfig.quickActions`; "Pick up where you left off" with Open, Publish (valid drafts with an unchanged address only)
  and Discard (with a confirm), all through `useDocumentOperation`.
- **Presentation locations**: `siteSettings`, `businessInfo` and `announcement` say "Shown on every page" in caution.

**Not done here.** Plan items 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 (the authoring kit, card 109, has the insert-menu thumbnails), 11 and 13.
`@sanity/themer` and its `themerTool()` stay a note for the next matched-set bump; nothing here needs them.

**Adopting it in a site.** Needs `@sanity/ui` 4 (card 103) and card 106. Copy the PORTABLE files, delete `StudioLogo.tsx`
and its `studio.components.logo` entry, take the `sanity.config.ts` lines, add the card-110 keys to `kit.config.ts`, the
`resolve.ts` entries for the site's shared types, and the guides map; check `public/favicon.svg` is the site's own mark.
Then `npm run test:unit` (the colour gate) and open `/studio`: the login screen shows the site's name, mark and
background in both schemes. Signed in, check the status line, Home and the help panel (the list is in `docs/PENDING.md`
item 15). Follow the marked-file order: starter first, then the site PR.

**Status, 2026-10-18.** Starter `yes` (login screen verified in a dev server; the signed-in views are unverified, see
PENDING item 15). Every other site `no`.

## Card 111: the Studio remembers: failed deploys, weekly ticks, Quick update, empty lists, restore-doc (2026-10-18)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn, where the pastor edits alone on Sanity's free plan (three days of history,
administrators only). Five gaps, each a support call waiting to happen. The status line compared only the build time with
the last publish, so a FAILED build said "taking longer than usual" for ever. "This week" could only tick what GROQ could
prove, so the jobs done outside the Studio (the church calendar, the bulletin printout) had nowhere to go. A phone edit
meant the full document form with the page builder in it. An empty desk list said "No documents of this type" and
nothing else. And "put the page back the way it was on Tuesday" had no answer at all once the history window closed.

**Canonical (PORTABLE):** `src/lib/deploy-status.ts` + `deploy-status.test.ts` (which also tests `studio-auth.ts`),
`src/lib/studio-auth.ts`, `src/pages/api/studio/deploy-status.ts`, `src/sanity/kit/weekType.ts`,
`src/sanity/kit/QuickUpdateTool.tsx`, `src/sanity/kit/emptyList.tsx`, `scripts/restore-doc.mjs`,
`scripts/lib/restore-doc.mjs` + `restore-doc.test.mjs`, and the card-111 changes to `kit/HomeTool.tsx`,
`kit/NavbarStatus.tsx`, `kit/shared.tsx`, `kit/index.tsx`, `kit/types.ts`, `src/lib/studio-kit.ts` (+ test) and
`docs/agent/studio-kit.md`. Per site (NOT portable): `kit.config.ts` (`thisWeek` hand and Checkup jobs,
`thisWeekTitle`, `quickUpdate` forms, `'quick-update'` in `staffTools`), `structure.ts` (`WEEK_TYPE` in the default-list hidden set, `emptyAwareList` on the
editor's lists), `wrangler.jsonc` (`vars.GITHUB_REPO`), `deploy.yml` and `publish-due.yml` (template changes below,
copied by hand), `package.json` (`restore:doc`), and the publish webhook's filter.

**What it adds.**

- **"The last update didn't go through."** `GET /api/studio/deploy-status/` reads the deploy workflow's newest runs
  from GitHub with a Worker secret (`GITHUB_DEPLOY_TOKEN`, Actions read and write on one repo), cached 60 seconds, and
  hands the Studio one word (`deployStatusFromRuns()`). A failure outranks the build-time comparison in the status line
  and Home's card, with "<helper> has been told" and **Try again**, a `POST` that needs the site's own origin and a
  Sanity session token checked against `/users/me` (`studio-auth.ts`), refuses while a deploy runs and within five
  minutes of the last, then dispatches the workflow. No token: `configured: false`, old behaviour.
- **"Has been told" is true:** the template `deploy.yml` now opens one `deploy-failed` issue on a failed run (or
  comments on the open one) and closes it on the next green run, so the owner gets GitHub's email.
- **Scheduled publishing rebuilds the site:** the template `publish-due.yml` reads `SANITY_API_WRITE_TOKEN` (not
  `SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN`, which the backup uses as a READ token) and, when a run published anything, starts `deploy.yml`
  with its own `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Its schedule stays commented out in the starter.
- **Weekly checklist.** `thisWeek` jobs can be `check: 'checkup'` (done when the Checkup has no "Needs doing") or
  `manual` (ticked by hand). Hand ticks are stored on one `studioWeek` document per week (`studioWeek-<first day>`),
  written straight to the dataset, skipped by Home's lists, the Checkup and the live check. Pure logic: `checklist()`,
  `weekKey()`, `weekDocId()`, tested. **The publish webhook's deny-list must add `"studioWeek"`**, or a tick rebuilds
  the site.
- **Quick update**, a tool for phones: `kitConfig.quickUpdate` forms (a few plain fields and a `build()` returning the
  whole document), opened one at a time with nothing else on screen, checked by `quickFormErrors()`, then created
  PUBLISHED. `build` (it may be async, and gets the client) must return a valid document because the Studio's
  validation is skipped.
- **Empty lists** say what goes there: `emptyAwareList()` for `structure.ts` (counts first; empty shows an explaining
  pane with "Create the first one"), and `EMPTY_LIST_BUNDLE` replacing Sanity's default empty words everywhere.
- **restore-doc.mjs**: one document from the newest (or a dated) nightly backup, via `gh`, decrypted in memory, a
  field-by-field summary, and with `--apply` (plus `NCS_PRODUCTION_WRITE=yes` on production) written back as a DRAFT.

**Adopting it in a site.** Needs cards 106 and 110. Copy the PORTABLE files, run `npm run typegen` (`studioWeek` is
new), add the `kit.config.ts` keys and the `structure.ts` wrappers, `vars.GITHUB_REPO` in `wrangler.jsonc`, the two
workflow changes, `"studioWeek"` in the webhook filter, then `npx wrangler secret put GITHUB_DEPLOY_TOKEN` and the
`SANITY_API_WRITE_TOKEN` repo secret. Follow the marked-file order: starter first, then the site PR.

**Status, 2026-10-18.** Starter `yes` (unit-tested; the kit's signed-out `/studio` checked in a dev server; signed-in
views unverified, PENDING item 17). first-baptist-auburn took it the same day. Every other site `no`.

**Follow-up, 2026-10-18 (signed-in walkthrough on first-baptist-auburn).** Quick update's submit button uses
`tone="primary"` (the positive tone drew a neon green that was off-brand on a reskinned theme; the green "saved"
card stays). `_seoFields.ts` titles read "Google title" and "Google description" instead of "SEO ..." (titles only,
field names unchanged). Both files are PORTABLE: copy them into a site that has card 111.

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** Applied on fbcm (no matrix column), presacademy, mas-monograms. On the other sites it is synced to starter a837dc3 only (synced, not individually verified).

## Card 112: React 19.3.1, one copy in the tree (2026-10-18)

**Origin:** the starter, PR #140 (`exp/react-19.3`, merged 2026-10-18 as `b5138b7`). Sanity 6.19 had already pulled
nested React 19.3.1 copies in under the family's exact 19.2.7 pin (`sanity`, `@sanity/ui`, `@sanity/visual-editing`,
`@sanity/cli-build`), so every site shipped two Reacts in its install tree, and `npm ci` printed an ERESOLVE warning
because `@portabletext/editor` 8.2.4 peers `react ^19.2.8`. Moving the pin to 19.3.1 collapses the tree to one copy.

**Canonical:** `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (NOT PORTABLE; each site moves its own pins). `react`,
`react-dom` and `react-is` exact at `19.3.1`, no caret. `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` stay on their carets
(`^19.2.x` resolves the current types; nothing to move). The rule text is `.claude/rules/dependencies.md` rule 8 and
card 13 (the exact-pin card this updates).

**What changed, measured in the starter:** gates, Playwright (120/120), `npm run build`, `wrangler dev` and the dev
Studio unchanged, same warnings. `scheduler` goes 0.27.0 to 0.28.0. The nested copies and the ERESOLVE warning are
gone. It also makes `@sanity/themer` installable (peers `react ^19.3.0`); the starter has it as a proof test only
(`src/lib/sanity-themer.test.ts`), not wired into the Studio, so sites do NOT take `@sanity/themer` with this card.

**Adopting it in a site.**

1. Worktree off `origin/main`. `npm install react@19.3.1 react-dom@19.3.1 react-is@19.3.1 --save-exact` on the
   committed lockfile (never delete or regenerate `package-lock.json`), then `npm ci`.
2. `npm ls react react-dom react-is` shows one version, every other line `deduped`.
3. Gates as separate commands: `npm run check`, `npm run build:full`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run sync-check`,
   `npm test`. One PR; merge when `build` and `test` are green; check the deployed site.

**Known, not caused by this card:** `astro dev` SSR logs `Invalid hook call` about seven times on first render, on
19.2.7 and 19.3.1 alike. It does not appear in `astro build` or the deployed site. Not investigated; leave it unless it
starts breaking a page.

**Status, 2026-10-18.** Starter `yes`. Rolled out the same day, one PR per site, each merged green and checked live
(the deployed bundles report React 19.3.1; Studio sign-in renders with a clean console): first-baptist-auburn #54,
fbcm #71, presacademy #105, reid-design-site #156, mas-monograms #116, stonesteps-50k #127, nixoncreativestudio #134
(no Sanity; it was on `^19.3.0` and is now exact, so card 13 is `yes` there too). `npm ls` showed one React in every
tree. presacademy and reid-design-site also took the starter's card-110 `checkPage.tsx` refactor in the same PR, because
their CI runs sync-check against the live starter and it had drifted that morning.

**Gotcha from the rollout:** two `astro build`s at once on one machine fail with `EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:9230` (the
workerd inspector port the prerender server opens). Run builds, and any Playwright config whose `webServer` builds,
one at a time.

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** The rollout report does not name this card per site. All five sites are synced to starter a837dc3 (synced, not individually verified).

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's Home audit (2026-10-17). Two small faults that every site in the family has.

1. **Faces cut off in CSS-cropped slots.** Many slots crop with `object-fit: cover` (a fixed-ratio card, a hero band)
   rather than asking Sanity for a cropped image, and CSS crops from the centre, so the head at the top of a phone
   photo is the part that goes. The editor's hotspot already says where the subject is; nothing read it.
2. **A church told Google it was a "$$" local business.** Site settings > Business type had no `Church`, and
   `localBusinessSchema()` emitted `priceRange: '$$'` for every type, which is noise for a church, a charity or a
   school.

**Canonical (not PORTABLE; copy by hand):**

- `src/components/SanityImage.astro`: when the image has a hotspot, an inline `style="object-position: X% Y%"` from
  `hotspot.x` / `hotspot.y`. A no-op for images not cropped by CSS, and an image without a hotspot renders exactly as
  before. A class that sets `object-position` loses to the inline style, so a slot that must pin its own position
  needs `!important` or a wrapper.
- `src/lib/schemas.ts`: `NON_SELLING_TYPES` (`Church`, `PlaceOfWorship`, `NGO`, `EducationalOrganization`) get no
  `priceRange`; every other type keeps `'$$'`.
- `src/sanity/schemaTypes/siteSettings.ts`: `Church` and `Place of Worship` added to the `businessType` list (the
  default stays `LocalBusiness`). A list change only, no data moves; run `npm run typegen` after copying it.

**Adopting it in a site.** Copy the three hunks, `npm run typegen`, build. A church site then sets Business type to
Church in the Studio (first-baptist-auburn went further: it defaults the field to Church and hides it). A site with its
own church JSON-LD (fbcm's `church-schema.ts` already emits `['Church', 'Organization']` with no price range) needs
only the SanityImage half.

**Status, 2026-10-18.** Starter `yes`. first-baptist-auburn has both (branch `claude/home-before-jacob`, PR #35).
fbcm: SanityImage half to adopt; JSON-LD half n/a. Crestview has no site repo, so n/a. Every other site `no`
(SanityImage half worth taking; the JSON-LD half changes nothing for a business).

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** Applied on presacademy, mas-monograms. On the other sites it is synced to starter a837dc3 only (synced, not individually verified).

## Card 114: publish-due.mjs takes the production write gate (2026-10-18)

**Origin:** stonesteps-50k, 2026-10-13 (its card 86 rollout, PR #117). Its `scripts/publish-due.mjs` gained the
second factor before the starter's did, so sync-check reported the site copy AHEAD of the starter. Ported back here.

**What was wrong.** Card 86 put the production second factor into `sanity-lib.mjs`, but `publish-due.mjs` cannot
import `sanity-lib` (that pulls in `@sanity/client`, and the publish-due workflow runs without `npm ci`). So a
local `node scripts/publish-due.mjs --apply` still published every due document in production on one flag.

**Canonical (PORTABLE):**

- `scripts/lib/write-gate.mjs` (new): `writeGate({ dataset, flag, ci, ciBare })` and `gateClient()`, node builtins
  only. Dry by default; on `production` a write needs the flag AND `NCS_PRODUCTION_WRITE=yes` in the process
  environment as it was when the module loaded; a `.env` that names the variable is refused. A script that opts in
  with `ci: true` may write inside GitHub Actions on its flag alone (the scheduled job has no person present, and
  its workflow file is reviewed code). The code is byte-for-byte stonesteps-50k's; only the header is generic.
- `scripts/publish-due.mjs`: `const APPLY = writeGate({ dataset, ci: true, quiet: true })`. In Actions the
  workflow's `--apply` still publishes, so no workflow changes. By hand, `--apply` alone now exits 2:
  `NCS_PRODUCTION_WRITE=yes node scripts/publish-due.mjs --apply`.

**Not PORTABLE:** `scripts/lib/write-gate.test.mjs`. Its `GATED` list is the site's own (the starter's names only
`publish-due.mjs`; stonesteps-50k lists 24 scripts). It runs in `test:scripts`, so CI and deploy cover it. The test
needs `@sanity/client` installed for its dummy-host probe; every site has it.

**Adopting it in a site.** Copy both PORTABLE files and the test (trim `GATED` to the scripts the site gates), run
`npm run test:scripts` and `node scripts/sync-check.mjs`. A site that checks against the live starter `main` in CI
(presacademy, first-baptist-auburn) goes red on its next run until it takes the copy, so per the Projects
`CLAUDE.md` order: this card's PR merges first, then each site's.

**Status, 2026-10-18.** Starter `yes`. stonesteps-50k `yes` (origin; it now takes the starter's header). fbcm (fbcm#73),
presacademy (presacademy#106) and first-baptist-auburn (fbc-auburn#58) took it the same day, each merged green. Sites with no `publish-due.mjs`
(reid-design-site, mas-monograms, nixoncreativestudio) `n/a`.

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** The rollout report does not name this card per site. All five sites are synced to starter a837dc3 (synced, not individually verified).
