## Card 135: Home's banner look is a style slot, and the hooks a site may select are documented and tested (2026-10-19)

**Origin:** the rollout of cards 128 to 134 to fbcm, presacademy, reid-design-site, mas-monograms and stonesteps-50k. All
five restyled Home's banner (and a few other kit surfaces) with a site CSS file that selected the kit's class names
(`.ncs-hb__go`, `.ncs-hb__who`, `.ncs-hb__motif`, `.ncs-ui .ui-banner__title`) and Sanity's markup (`[data-ui='Stack']`,
`[data-ui='Button']`, `h1[data-ui='Heading']`). A kit rename would have switched each look off with no failing test.

**PORTABLE, new:** `src/lib/studio-banner-style.ts` (the type, the checks, the shape CSS, the hook lists),
`src/lib/studio-banner-style.test.ts` (the gate), `src/sanity/kit/harness/bannerLooks.ts` (the five sites' looks as slot
entries: the test's proof of coverage and the migration recipes).

**PORTABLE, changed:** `src/sanity/kit/HomeBanner.tsx` (the `data-hb-part` attributes, the resolved style, the stamp),
`src/sanity/kit/types.ts` (`HomeBannerConfig.style`), `src/sanity/kit/harness/Harness.tsx` (`?view=banner&look=<key>`),
`docs/agent/studio-kit.md` ("Home's banner style" and the migration notes).

**Per site, not portable:** `kit.config.ts` `homeBanner.style`, when a site wants a look. Nothing else: no site CSS.

**What it changes.** `homeBanner.style` sets the date line (words with `{date}`, face, size, weight, tracking, case,
colour, a hairline or dot before it), the greeting (face, italic), the title (face, size, leading, case, colour, a hard
echo, an outlined last letter), the button (shape `pill`, `square`, `tag`, `plate` or `stitched`, its colours and
words), the background (colour, texture, a line along the foot), where the motif sits (`foot` or `behind-right`) and a
stamp. Every value is checked: colours must be hex and read on the banner (4.5:1 for the date line and the button's
words, 3:1 for large text and marks), fonts and lengths are stripped of anything that could close a rule, and a value
that fails is dropped and named in `resolveBannerStyle().notes`. The only markup a site may select beyond the config is
`data-hb-part` (13 names), the `data-hb-*` state attributes and the `--hb-*` variables, all listed in `studio-kit.md`.
With no style the banner is byte for byte what it was.

**Why `kitConfig.homeBanner.style` and not `brand.config.json` `studio.look`.** The style changes the same elements as
`homeBanner.mark`, `motif`, `accent` and `lettering`, which already live in `kit.config.ts`; it is TypeScript, so a
wrong key fails `npm run check`; and a banner's face and button are not devices the whole Studio shares, which is what
`studio.look` is for.

**Gates.** Unit (`studio-banner-style.test.ts`): no style emits nothing; every documented part is in HomeBanner.tsx and
every part in it is documented; a full style produces every documented attribute and variable; the static CSS selects
every attribute; the docs list every part, attribute and variable; each of the five sites' looks resolves with no ignored
value and every chip shape is used; the contrast and injection guards. Kit bench `/kit-harness/guide/?view=banner&look=none|fbcm|presacademy|reid|mas|stonesteps`
at 1280 and 375: no horizontal scroll, each look draws.

**Not covered, and why:** the other kit surfaces sites restyle by class name (`.ui-eyebrow`, the Site Guide's list, the
splash). docs/PENDING.md item 31.

**Applied to:** ncs-astro-sanity-starter (canonical), first-baptist-auburn (branch, 2026-10-19; Auburn sets no style).

**Rolled out, 2026-10-19.** Applied on fbcm (no matrix column), presacademy, reid-design-site, mas-monograms, stonesteps-50k.

## Card 136: Home's Visitors card reads Google Analytics 4, and a Search Console card, through studio-status (2026-10-19)

**Origin:** fbcm, presacademy, reid-design-site, mas-monograms, stonesteps-50k and nixoncreativestudio count visitors
with GA4 (`PUBLIC_GA_ID`), not Cloudflare Web Analytics, so card 115's Visitors card said "Not set up yet" there. Nathan
wanted their GA4 numbers on Home the way Site Kit shows them on his WordPress sites, plus Search Console.

**Design.** No Google key in any site Worker. The studio's own Worker, studio-status (NateJ45/studio-status), already
holds the studio's read-only service account (`GA4_SA_KEY`, GA4 Viewer on every property, Restricted on the Search
Console properties). It gains a `SiteData` `WorkerEntrypoint` (`src/site-data.ts` there, NateJ45/studio-status#18)
with `siteAnalytics(siteKey, requests)` and `searchConsole(siteKey, queries)`, a site-key-to-property map and a 3-hour
cache. A site binds `SITE_DATA` to it and names itself with `SITE_DATA_KEY`. RPC is reachable only through a binding in
the same account, so it needs no token or allow-list. The site builds the report bodies and maps the answers (tested
here); studio-status adds only the property, the token and the cache.

**PORTABLE, new:** `src/lib/studio-google.ts` (which source, the binding call, the GA4 batch and its mapping onto
`VisitorsReport`, the Search Console queries and `SearchReport`, the plain words), `src/pages/api/studio/search.ts`
(the Search Console route), `src/lib/google-auth.ts` (the OPTIONAL fallback: a service-account JWT signed with
WebCrypto inside the site Worker, for a site outside the studio's account), and the tests `studio-google.test.ts` and
`google-auth.test.ts`.

**PORTABLE, changed:** `src/pages/api/studio/visitors.ts` (picks Cloudflare or GA4, the connect state, thirty-minute
cache for Google), `src/lib/studio-analytics.ts` (`VisitorsReport.provider`), `src/sanity/kit/HomeCards.tsx` (the GA4
small print, `ConnectGoogle`, `SearchConsole` and `SearchBody` drawn under Visitors), `src/sanity/kit/harness/Surfaces.tsx`
(`part=google`), `docs/agent/studio-kit.md` ("Google Analytics and Search Console").

**Per site, not portable:** `wrangler.jsonc` (the `SITE_DATA` service binding, entrypoint `SiteData`, and the
`SITE_DATA_KEY` var; commented in the template), `.dev.vars.example`, and the site's entry in studio-status.

**Settings.** `SITE_DATA` (service binding to `studio-status`, entrypoint `SiteData`), `SITE_DATA_KEY` (`fbcm`,
`presacademy`, `reid`, `mas`, `stonesteps`, `ncs`), `ANALYTICS_PROVIDER` (`cloudflare` | `ga4`; unset means
whichever is set up, Cloudflare first, so card 115 sites do not move). Fallback only: secret `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`,
vars `GA4_PROPERTY_ID` and `SEARCH_CONSOLE_SITE`; the binding wins when both are present.

**What it changes.** With GA4 picked, the Visitors card shows sessions as visits, day by day, the most-read pages and
how people found the site, from one `batchRunReports`. GA4's own "AI Assistant" channel (and the `ai-assistant`
medium) feeds the AI assistants group directly; a source-name list (chatgpt, perplexity, copilot, gemini, claude and the
rest) is the fallback. The small print says "From Google Analytics, updated a few hours ago". A "Found on Google" card

ago against the 28 before, the average place, "Searches that found you" and the pages Google sent people to; hidden
when not set up, including when studio-status has no Search Console property for the site. A Google 401/403, a key
studio-status does not know or a broken fallback key shows "Ask <helper> to finish connecting Google", never detail.
Both routes check same origin, then a Sanity member, then the settings, and cache thirty minutes per Worker instance.
No new cookies, nothing new on the public site.

**Gates.** Unit: `studio-google.test.ts` (the provider pick with and without the binding, a mock `SiteData` binding:
the request bodies and site key it receives, the mapped answers, `not-set-up` keeping the card hidden, `connect`,

`google-auth.test.ts` (a throwaway RSA key made in the test: the JWT verifies, the claims and scopes, the token cache,

## Card 138: CI builds from a pinned content snapshot, and a scheduled live-watch checks the real site (2026-10-19)

**Origin:** the church (fbcm) renamed its Staff page slug to `ministers` in the Studio. fbcm CI built against the LIVE
dataset and its tests named `/staff`, so `build`, `test`, the e2e shards and the link check all went red on a docs-only
PR. Sites are handed to clients; an editor renaming a page must never turn CI red or block a merge or a deploy. fbcm's
earlier attempt (rewriting 24 specs to be content-agnostic plus an `@content` watch) was set aside: it touches every test
in every repo and still reads live content. Pinning the content removes the coupling for all of them at once.

**PORTABLE, new:** `scripts/snapshot.mjs` (`export`, `serve`, `run -- <cmd>`; a groq-js query server over a committed
`ci/sanity-snapshot.ndjson.gz`, answering `/v<ver>/data/query/<dataset>` GET and POST; `snapshotClientOptions(env)`),
`scripts/lib/snapshot.test.mjs`, `scripts/live-watch.mjs`, `.github/workflows/live-watch.yml`. `groq-js` 2.0.0 is a
devDependency (already in the tree through `sanity`; pinned to that version).

**Per site, not portable:** `ci/sanity-snapshot.ndjson.gz` (the data); a one-line spread in `src/lib/sanity.ts`
(`snapshotUrl`), in `cmsQuery` of `astro.config.mjs` where it exists, and in every build-time script that calls
`createClient`; `ci.yml`, `lighthouse.yml`, `visual.yml` wrap their build in `node scripts/snapshot.mjs run --`;
the `SITE_URL` repo variable and the `live-watch.yml` schedule; `CLAUDE.md` / tests rules and the test inventory.

**What it changes.** CI reads the published documents as of the last `export`, through a local server, with no token and
no network to Sanity for documents. `deploy.yml` is untouched: production builds live. Required checks keep their names;
nothing in the shape of `ci.yml` changes except the build command. A tests-name-a-page fixture is now stable until the
snapshot is refreshed, and the refresh is a deliberate PR of ours. `live-watch` is the replacement for noticing a break:
daily, not required, never on a PR, and a red scheduled run mails the owner.

**Gates.** `scripts/lib/snapshot.test.mjs` (options, ndjson, params, a GET and POST round trip, a bad query is a 400).
Proof per site: build from the snapshot, then `npm run parity compare` where a parity baseline exists, and a throwaway
rename (snapshot copy with a page slug changed in the editor's way) that leaves `build` and `test` green.

**Not covered, and why:** images and files are still fetched from cdn.sanity.io (a deleted asset could 404 in a
screenshot test); the snapshot can go stale, which only matters when a deliberate refresh is needed; Studio-side
behaviour is not content-dependent. Detail: `docs/claude/build-and-scripts.md`.

**Follow-up (2026-10-19):** `live-watch.mjs` treats a missing `<h1>` as a warning, not a failure. The first live run on fbcm found `/visitor/` without one, and a daily red run for a nicety would have been muted.

**Applied to:** ncs-astro-sanity-starter (canonical), stonesteps-50k, reid-design-site, fbcm (2026-10-19). Measured and not coupled (CI already builds on the empty placeholder, nothing to pin): presacademy, mas-monograms, first-baptist-auburn (only its non-required visual workflow reads live ids).

## Card 151: starter component type fixes from the FBC Auburn standardising pass (2026-10-24)

**Origin:** FBC Auburn measured type, spacing and overflow on every route with Playwright and found four bugs in components that came unchanged from the starter. (1) `FaqAccordion.tsx`: the questions rendered at 16px, because `AccordionTrigger` merges its classes through `cn` (tailwind-merge), which reads the custom `text-h3` as a colour and drops it beside `text-foreground`; now `text-[length:var(--text-h3)]`. Any custom `text-<token>` size passed through `cn` beside a `text-<colour>` has the same trap. (2) Labels and chips at `text-[0.62rem]` to `text-[0.7rem]` (about 10 to 11px) are now `text-xs`, the 12px floor: `StatsCounter.tsx`, `Header.astro`, `JournalCard.astro`, `FeaturedJournal.astro`, `FeaturedWork.astro`, `BeforeAfterSlider.tsx`, `JournalCategoryChip.astro`, `ProjectCard.astro`, `Provisional.astro`. (3) `sections/LogoStrip.astro`: the row layout was `overflow-x-auto` with `justify-center`, so when the logos overflowed, the first one sat off the left edge where scrolling cannot reach; now `justify-center-safe`. (4) `JournalPortableText.tsx`: body headings were at full section size with section-sized space above (an H2 was `text-h2` under `mt-section-lg`); they now sit one step down (H2 `text-h3 mt-l mb-s`, H3 `text-h4 mt-l mb-xs`, H4 `text-h5 mt-m mb-xs`), the pull quote uses `my-l py-l`, and the em-dash before its attribution is gone (public copy rule). **Not ported:** Auburn-only radius tokens, and its `.c-facts` and `.board-rule-wrap` fixes (the starter has neither). None of these files is `PORTABLE`, so a site takes the change by hand: grep for the same class strings. No config, no schema change.

## Card 152: Church Trac on a church site (2026-10-24, a pattern card, no starter code)

**Origin:** fbcm moved from Planning Center to Church Trac (2026-09-24 and 25) and built three pieces; FBC Auburn (also on Church Trac) took them on 2026-10-24 so its Contact, Prayer and "Tell us you are coming" forms deliver into Church Trac instead of needing a form backend. **Decided:** the starter has no church layer, so the code stays in the church sites; this card is the map for the next church site. Sanity stays the CMS for page copy; Church Trac feeds what it owns.

1. **Church systems boxes and link tokens.** Every outside address (giving, connection card, contact and prayer forms, calendar, app, member sign-in) is one https box in Site settings, and a link field can hold a token such as `{giving}` or `{connect}` that the build fills when it is the whole link value. A blank box falls back to the site's own page (`/give/`, `/contact/`), never a broken link, and the build logs it. fbcm fills at its fetch chokepoint (`settings-placeholders.ts`); Auburn fills in its own `queries.ts` wrapper so the PORTABLE `sanity.ts` is untouched. Link fields need a rule that accepts a known token (fbcm `_linkRule.ts`).
2. **Church Trac form band.** Staff paste Church Trac's embed code; only an https churchtrac.com iframe address survives (`church-trac-form.ts`, pure, shared by the Studio validation and the component), and the site draws its own frame plus an "open in a new tab" link. Auburn also swaps its own Contact and Prayer forms for the Church Trac form automatically once the box is filled.
3. **Church Trac page reader.** Church Trac has no feed or API for its pages, so `church-trac-page.ts` reads a published page's HTML (a hundred-line tokenizer, no dependency), keeps headings, paragraphs, images, buttons and columns, drops template text and unsafe links, and the site draws it in its own type. One fetch per page per build, two tries, failure logged and shown as "Read it on Church Trac"; a daily rebuild keeps it within a day. Test against saved real pages (fbcm's `tests/fixtures/churchtrac-*.html`), never the live site in CI. fbcm hard-codes its two newsletters; Auburn makes it a band that names the page.

**Where it lives:** fbcm `src/lib/church-links.ts`, `church-trac-form.ts`, `church-trac-page.ts`, `church-trac-newsletters.ts`, `OPERATIONS.md` "Switching to Church Trac"; FBC Auburn `docs/agent/church-trac.md`. **Also:** the iCal calendar (`church-calendar.ts`) is the fourth Church Trac feed, already in both sites.

## Card 153: a build-time script-src for the public pages (2026-10-24)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's mobile Lighthouse report flagged its CSP as missing `script-src` and `object-src`
("Ensure CSP is effective against XSS"). Astro's own `security.csp` does not support `<ClientRouter />`, and the router
runs the next page's inline scripts under the FIRST page's policy, so a per-page policy cannot work either. Built in
first-baptist-auburn (NateJ45/fbc-auburn#140), then generalised here.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE: `scripts/build-csp.mjs`, `scripts/lib/csp.mjs` (+ `csp.test.mjs`). Per site (NOT portable):
the `/*` `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'` line and the `/studio/*` detach rule in `public/_headers`,
the `npm run build` chain in `package.json`, the optional `scripts/csp-origins.json` (a JSON array of extra origins),
and the "Security headers" section of `docs/agent/deployment.md` plus the note in `docs/agent/custom-code.md`.

**What it does.** `npm run build` is now `with-workerd astro build && node scripts/build-csp.mjs && node
scripts/build-search-index.mjs`. The script reads every built page in `dist/client` (not `/studio`), including the
documents inside Custom code `srcdoc` frames (they inherit the page's policy), and rewrites the `/*` rule's CSP line in
`dist/client/_headers` to `frame-ancestors 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; script-src ...`. The list is
`'self'`, `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (Pagefind's WebAssembly; it allows wasm compilation, never JS eval), every external
`<script src>` origin, GA4's `googletagmanager.com` when a page carries the tag, the site's `csp-origins.json`, one
sorted sha256 per inline script on any page, `'unsafe-hashes'` plus hashes if an inline `on*=` handler exists, and
`'unsafe-inline'` last (ignored by any browser that understands hashes; only a pre-hash browser reads it). JSON-LD and
other non-running script types are skipped. `default-src` is deliberately unset, so images, frames, styles, fonts and
fetches are untouched. The build FAILS if the placeholder line is missing, so the policy never silently drops to none.
`/studio/*` detaches the policy (`! Content-Security-Policy`, then `frame-ancestors 'self'` only; card 59 trap 1).
Trusted Types are not required: enforcing them breaks the router, Pagefind and the React islands.

**Verified in the starter (2026-10-24)** under `npm run build` then `npm run preview` (wrangler dev): a page carries the
full policy, `/studio/` carries `frame-ancestors 'self'` only, a `/_astro/*` file carries the full policy (no effect on a script
response) and keeps its immutable cache line, nine pages in a row through the router, search (switched on locally for the check), the Custom code wall at `/styleguide/sections/` and the Studio load with no CSP violations, and
`npm run test:unit` passes. fbc-auburn measured Lighthouse best-practices 100 with it.

**Applied:** starter (this card); first-baptist-auburn (origin, fbc-auburn#140; PORTABLE copies since fbc-auburn#147,
2026-10-24, sync-check clean). fbcm and Crestview are not matrix columns: fbcm sends only `frame-ancestors` today and can
take it as-is.

**Who should take it.** As-is (their `_headers` still say only `frame-ancestors 'self'`): stonesteps-50k, fbcm, and
mas-monograms (its line lists extra frame-ancestors origins, so either drop them, as the Studio is embedded, or change
`PLACEHOLDER` to match). presacademy, reid-design-site and nixoncreativestudio already send a full policy with
`script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ...`, which Lighthouse rates as not effective; they want the hashes too, but their
`script-src` lives inside a `default-src` policy, so that port needs `build-csp.mjs` to rewrite only the `script-src`
directive (a small extension to this card, decide when the first of them is ported). wcp, 2ndpreschicago and
ncs-church-starter are archived.

**Known, harmless console error (found live on fbc-auburn, 2026-10-24):** on an in-site click, Astro's router appends an
empty `data:application/javascript,` module script after a page's last inline module, only to wait for it. The policy
blocks it and the console logs a CSP error; the router resolves on `onerror` too, so nothing breaks, and a first load
(what Lighthouse measures) never does it. Decided: leave `data:` out of `script-src`. A port check that sees only this
error has passed. Detail: `docs/agent/deployment.md`, "Security headers".

**Gotcha:** a widget that pasted code adds AT RUNTIME from a host that is not in the HTML (a loader that pulls a second
script) is blocked. Put its origin in `scripts/csp-origins.json` and rebuild. Verify every port under `npm run preview`,
never a plain static server: only wrangler applies `_headers`.

## Card 154: search reads uploaded files, forgives typos, knows the site's words (2026-10-25)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn asked for search "as robust and complete as possible". Card 126's Pagefind index read
only page HTML, so a bulletin PDF was found by its title alone; Pagefind 1.5 has no fuzzy matching ("baptsim" found
nothing), no synonyms, and a multi-word search where one word matched nothing returned nothing. Built here first.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE: `scripts/build-search-index.mjs`, `scripts/lib/search-files.mjs` (+ `search-files.test.mjs`),
`src/lib/site-search.ts` (+ test), `src/lib/site-search-client.ts`, `src/components/search/SearchPanel.astro`,
`tests/search.spec.ts`. Per site (NOT portable): `site.search.synonyms` in `src/data/site.ts`, the
`data-search-*` attributes on a site's own file links, and the `actions/cache` step in `ci.yml` (site job),
`deploy.yml` and `lighthouse.yml`. New exact-pinned devDependencies: `unpdf` 1.8.1 and `mammoth` 1.13.0, used only at
build time and imported only when a page links a file of that kind.

**What it does.**

1. **Files.** After `astro build`, every link to `cdn.sanity.io/files/...` (or a same-site `.pdf`/`.docx`/`.txt`)
   inside an indexed `<main>` becomes its own Pagefind record: the text read out of the file, led by its title and
   optional note, with type, date, format ("PDF") and the linking page as "From ...". Files come from the BUILT PAGES,
   never from a Sanity query, so expired, scheduled, private and noindex files stay out with no extra logic. Links can
   carry `data-search-title`, `data-search-type` (`bulletin`, `notes`, `newsletter`, `form`, `policy`, `download`), `data-search-date`
   and `data-search-note`; a bare link still works (type `file`, title from its text). A file that will not
   download (20 s timeout), is over 25 MB or is a scan (under 10 characters a page) is indexed by
   title only and logged once; the build never fails over a file. Audio, images and other formats are left out unless the link carries `data-search-title`. Text is cached by the Sanity SHA-1 in
   `node_modules/.cache/search-files/`, kept by `actions/cache`, so a file is read once ever. The asset URLs are
   immutable, so CI reading them does not break card 138.
2. **"Did you mean".** The build counts every indexed word into `dist/client/pagefind/words.json` (top 20k). With no
   results, the client fetches it once, corrects each unknown word to the nearest frequent one (1 edit up to six
   letters, 2 beyond, swaps count as one, never a prefix of a real word), searches that and says so: "Nothing found for
   "baptsim". Showing 4 results for "baptism"." plus a "Search for "baptsim" instead" button.
3. **Other ways to say it.** Under three results, the client also searches the site's synonym groups and spelled-out
   Bible books ("Jn 3" -> "John 3", "1cor" -> "1 Corinthians"; names like "Tim" change only before a chapter), and with
   none, each meaningful word alone. Results merge by Pagefind id, the original search's results first.

**Verified in the starter (2026-10-25):** `npm run test:unit` (fixture PDF, blank "scanned" PDF and DOCX are built
inside the test, no binaries committed), `npm run check`. End to end on first-baptist-auburn's real content: see its PR.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin, see the status line added with its PR.

**Who should take it.** Any site with `search.enabled` (today only first-baptist-auburn). Others take it with card 126.

## Card 155: Print stylesheet and the regex-backslash guard (2026-10-25)

**Origin.** first-baptist-auburn, PR #170 (audit 2026-10-25, two findings).

**Canonical (PORTABLE-marked).** `scripts/lib/regex-backslash.mjs`, `scripts/lib/regex-backslash.test.mjs`.
Not marked: `src/styles/print.css` (each site lists its own start-hidden classes) and `tests/print.spec.ts` (Auburn's
copy also pins its own `beforeprint` handler and extra routes).

**What it does.**

1. **Regex-backslash guard.** Git Bash heredocs on this PC strip backslashes, so `/(\s+)/` written through one becomes
   `/(s+)/`: valid JavaScript that silently matches the letter s. The detector scans every tracked `.ts`, `.tsx`,
   `.mjs`, `.js` and `.astro` file (frontmatter and `<script>` bodies) with the TypeScript scanner and fails the
   `test:scripts` run on a backslash-free regex or `new RegExp('...')` that still holds `s+`, `d{2}`, `[^s]` and the
   like. Passes on the starter as it stands (nothing to fix).
2. **Print stylesheet.** `src/styles/print.css`, imported last in `BaseLayout.astro`, on top of the minimal print block
   in `globals.css`. Print never scrolls, so `[data-reveal]`, `[data-stagger-grid]` children, `.hero-entry-stagger`,
   the image curtain and the process connector stayed on their hidden starting state and a printed page went blank
   below the first screen. Print now shows them finished, drops the hero slideshow and iframes, and prints `main`
   black on white (background fills are not printed, so light-on-dark text vanished). `tests/print.spec.ts`
   print-emulates every route in `tests/routes.ts` and fails when text in `<main>` would print invisible, plus one
   test that proves a reveal really is hidden on screen and shown in print.

**Not ported.** `src/lib/flow-split.ts` (the starter has no word splitter; it is Auburn's flow layer). Auburn's
`beforeprint` handler in `motion.ts` (no equivalent script here; the CSS alone covers it). Auburn's brand-specific
print rules (brick slabs, Sunday bar, placeholder notes, building sketch). Known gap: `StatsCounter` counts up from 0
on scroll, so it prints 0 until scrolled into view.

**Applied.** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: source (applied). Other sites take the two guard files
byte-identical and write their own `print.css` from the starter's, extending layer 1 with their own reveal classes.

## Card 156: contact form posts safely without JS, one-pass errors, kept drafts; FAQ landmark; focus rings on dark bands (2026-10-25)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's 2026-10-25 audit (Auburn PRs 170 and 173). Four findings that are not church
specific: a contact form that sent its answers to the address bar with scripting off, a form that stopped at the first
problem, a draft left in localStorage on shared computers, a second "Common questions" landmark inside an already
labelled section, and a focus ring that nearly vanished on the near-black band.

**Canonical:** none new. Changed, all "Safe to edit" or "Foundation" in the starter, so sites take them by hand:
`src/components/ContactForm.tsx`, `src/components/FaqAccordion.tsx`, `src/pages/contact.astro`,
`src/lib/surfaces.ts` (+ `surfaces.test.ts`), `src/styles/globals.css`, new `tests/contact-form.spec.ts`.

**What it does.**

1. **No JavaScript.** The form is `method="post" action="/api/contact/"`, so scripting off never turns the answers
   into a GET query string. `/api/contact/` (PORTABLE, left alone) reads JSON only, so a plain post still gets a 400:
   `contact.astro` therefore carries a `<noscript>` notice that points at the email and phone. A real no-JS send
   needs the endpoint to accept a form-encoded body and redirect; that is a change to a PORTABLE file and is a
   separate card.
2. **Every problem in one pass.** `validate()` also covers the editor-written questions (required, email shape), each
   field gets `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` for its own line, and an error summary (`role="alert"`,
   `tabindex="-1"`) takes focus after a failed submit and links to each field. Every required label carries the
   same `*` (`RequiredCue`) with a one-line key above the form.
3. **Draft.** Kept in `sessionStorage` (this tab only, wrapped in try/catch), cleared on success; a draft an older
   build left in `localStorage` is removed on load. Answers to editor-written questions are still not kept (the editor
   can reword them at any time).
4. **Prefill.** `/contact/?topic=<word>` picks the first list answer containing the word (hyphens read as spaces; the
   project type on the built-in form, the first list question on an editor-written one) and `&about=<short text>`
   starts the message with "About <text>: ". Control characters are stripped and the text is cut at 80 characters.
   Nothing the visitor typed is overwritten.
5. **FAQ landmark.** `FaqAccordion` renders a `<section aria-labelledby>` only when a category heading exists; with no
   category the wrapper is a plain `<div>`, because the section that holds it is already the labelled region (axe
   `landmark-unique`).
6. **Dark-band rings.** `globals.css` sets `--ring` to the band's light ink inside `[data-dark-surface]` and the Ink band
   (`.bg-accent-dark`); the Feature band already did. `data-light-surface` opts a light card back out.
   `surfaces.ts` gains `ring`, and `surfaces.test.ts` holds each dark band's ring to 3:1 in both themes and checks
   that `globals.css` really sets it. A new dark section adds `data-dark-surface`.

**Not ported:** Auburn's "planning to visit" line (`?visit=sunday-11`), its `btn-auburn` button classes, the Auburn
white and navy ring literals (the starter uses its own tokens), the heading size and `--heading-solid` edits in
`FaqAccordion`, and the Home hero / board selectors that carried `--ring` in `auburn.css`.

**Verified in the starter (2026-10-25):** see the PR for the gate output (check, build, unit, `contact-form.spec.ts`).

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn = source (applied).

**Who should take it.** Every site with a contact form or an FAQ. Sites with their own dark bands add
`data-dark-surface`.

## Card 157: The phone menu on a native dialog, one dropdown model, transform-only header compaction (2026-10-25)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's 2026-10-25 UX and web-dev audits (Auburn PR #174, "chrome", and the later
header-shake fix in its `Header.astro`). The phone menu was a shadcn Sheet (Radix Dialog) React island on every page;
a hover-opened dropdown snapped shut when its label was clicked; and Auburn's compacting header changed height, so
scroll anchoring moved `scrollY` back across a single 8px threshold and the bar shook near the top.

**Canonical:** no new PORTABLE files. Every file here is a per-site Foundation file each site has already reskinned:
`src/components/MobileNav.astro` (new, replaces the deleted `MobileNav.tsx`), `src/components/Header.astro`, the
"Header compaction" and "Mobile menu" blocks in `src/styles/globals.css`, and `id="site-footer"` on the footer in
`src/components/Footer.astro`. A site copies the behaviour, not the bytes.

**What it does.**

1. **Phone menu on `<dialog>`.** `MobileNav.astro` is server markup: the hamburger and every link are in the HTML, and
   no Radix or React runtime ships for it. `showModal()` gives the focus trap, Escape, the inert page and focus back on
   the hamburger; a small delegated script (bound once, survives View Transitions) opens it and closes it on the X,
   the backdrop (a click whose target is the dialog itself), any link inside, and `astro:before-preparation`.
   `html:has(.mobile-menu[open])` locks the page scroll. The panel slides in from the right with a transform; the global
   reduced-motion reset flattens it. "Search the site" closes the menu, then fires `site-search:open`, with
   `stopImmediatePropagation()` so the search dialog's own click listener does not shut it again. With JS off the
   hamburger is a link to `#site-footer`. The starter's layout, nav data, groups, CTA and theme toggle (the same
   `ThemeToggle client:idle` the eyebrow strip uses) are kept. The `site-header__menu` hook class is kept, so the
   `minimal` header variant still shows the menu at desktop widths.
2. **One dropdown model.** Mouse hover opens a group; clicking a label hover just opened keeps it open (a second click
   closes); leaving starts a 300ms close cancelled on return; tap, Enter and Space toggle the native `<details>`
   (`e.detail === 0` for the keyboard); Escape closes and returns focus to the label. Still server-rendered (rule 4).
3. **Header compaction, transforms only.** Past 64px of scroll the header gets `data-scrolled`, cleared only at 8px or
   less (the hysteresis that stops the shake). From lg up the bar slides up by the stripe plus eyebrow height (measured
   into `--hdr-top`) plus `--spacing-m`, its row contents slide down by half of that, and the logo scales 48 to 40px:
   the bar keeps its layout height, so nothing under it reflows. Below lg it only gains a shadow. The existing
   hide-on-scroll-down (`data-state="hidden"`) still wins.

**Not ported:** Auburn's church groups, This Sunday card, Live now row, Give button, brick sill and big-serif full-screen
sheet (church-only design); the "Menu" pill and `data-nav-complete` (Auburn hides the pill when the desktop row lists
every page; the starter's desktop never shows the hamburger except in the `minimal` variant); the Home `data-past`
logo swap (Auburn's Home hero only). `src/components/ui/sheet.tsx` stays: nothing in the starter imports the Sheet now,
but it is part of the shadcn set; `radix-ui` is still used by the other primitives, and nothing was uninstalled.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn = source (applied).

**Who should take it.** Every site still on `MobileNav.tsx`: swap in `MobileNav.astro` restyled to the site, the dropdown
script and the compaction block. Check the site's own header CSS for height or padding transitions first.

## Card 158: One accent button per page, named section anchors, a 404 with search, calendar files (2026-10-25)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's 2026-10-25 audit (its PRs #171, #172, #173): pages with several filled accent
buttons where none stood out, sections nobody could link to, a 404 with no way to search, and per-gathering `.ics`
files. Generalised here.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE: `src/lib/cta-budget.ts` (+ test), `src/lib/section-anchors.ts` (+ test), `src/lib/ics.ts`
(+ test). Per site (NOT portable): the wiring in `SectionRenderer.astro` (which blocks draw a primary button, the
`anchors` prop), the `primaryVariant` prop on `Hero.astro` and `FinalCta.astro`, and `src/pages/404.astro`.

**What it does.**

1. **One accent button.** `primaryBudget(rows, drawsPrimary)` gives the first section that draws a primary button
   (a hero with a main button, or a closing band) the `primary` variant and every later one `secondary`;
   `SectionRenderer` passes it to `Hero` and `FinalCta` as `primaryVariant`. A renderer concern, so blocks still carry
   no colour field (rule 9). A Hero or FinalCta drawn outside the renderer is not counted.
2. **Named anchors.** `sectionAnchors()` gives every section with a heading (`heading`, else `headline`) a unique id
   made from it (`/about/#our-story`), stega stripped so the preview matches the live page, cut to 48 characters at a
   word break, prefixed `section-` before a digit, `-2`/`-3` on a repeat, never one of `RESERVED_IDS` or another
   section's numbered id. Unnamed sections keep `<idPrefix>-<n>`. `overrides` pins a name to a block `_key` (Auburn's
   `SECTION_ANCHORS` map plugs in there). The styleguide pages pass `anchors="numbered"`, since they draw one renderer
   per fixture.
3. **404 with search.** With `site.search.enabled`, a plain GET form to `/search/?q=` (works without JavaScript);
   under it, search on or off, the site's `site.search.suggestions` as "Pages people often look for".
4. **Calendar files.** `buildIcs()`: escaping, 75-octet folding that never splits a character, CRLF, typed or raw
   RRULE, TZID wall times with VTIMEZONE for the four US zones, UTC instants, all-day dates. No route in the starter;
   the file's header shows the `src/pages/calendar/[key].ics.ts` endpoint a site adds.

**Not ported:** Auburn's gatherings (Church facts service times, `src/lib/gatherings.ts`, the `/calendar/<key>.ics`
route), because the starter has no recurring gatherings. Its only event-like content is the RSVP block (`startsAt`, a
UTC instant), a natural first consumer, not wired here. Auburn's "navy" quiet variant and its extra primary-button
blocks (steps rail, walk) are site-specific; its 404 brick path is brand art.

**Auburn can adopt the libs:** `gatheringIcs()` maps onto `buildIcs({ events: [{ start: { date, time, tzid:
'America/New_York' }, duration: 'PT1H', rrule: { freq: 'WEEKLY', byDay: [day] }, ... }] })` and gains line folding
(its long LOCATION lines are not folded today); `anchorFor()` becomes `sectionAnchors(..., { overrides:
SECTION_ANCHORS })`, which also names its other sections from their headings, so check its pages' links first.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn = source: it takes `src/lib/ics.ts` (+ test) byte-identical, and its `gatheringIcs()` now builds on `buildIcs()` (long LOCATION lines are folded); it keeps its own `src/lib/section-anchors.ts` (a key map with a different API, unmarked, a recorded fork) and its own button budget in `SectionRenderer.astro` (the navy variant), so it does not carry `cta-budget.ts`.

## Card 159: page weight, cache and security headers, share images (2026-10-25)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's site audit (fbc-auburn#176 CSP, #177 performance). Every page inlined the CSS
of every component its module graph reached, about half of it dead; the build-time CSP line from card 153 grew with
every small component script until it passed Cloudflare's 2,000-character limit for a `_headers` line and a deploy
failed (gotcha `cloudflare-headers-line-limit-breaks-hashed-csp`); a noindex page still named a canonical; share
images from Sanity could be WebP.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE: `scripts/purge-page-css.mjs`, `scripts/lib/css-purge.mjs` (+ `css-purge.test.mjs`). Per site
(NOT portable): the `build` script order in `package.json`, `public/_headers`, `astro.config.mjs`, `BaseLayout.astro`.

**What it does.**

1. **Per-page CSS purge.** `npm run build` runs `purge-page-css.mjs` after `astro build` and before `build-csp.mjs`
   (the CSP hashes scripts only, so the order does not change it). For each built page it drops every inline style
   rule whose selector needs a class found nowhere in the page's HTML or its scripts (followed through imports).
   Rules without classes, `:not()`, `@font-face`, `@keyframes` and other at-rules are never touched; a script that
   builds class names from pieces lists a prefix in `KEEP`. **Measured on the starter (16 pages):** with the default
   `inlineStylesheets: 'auto'` only 11 KB of CSS is inline in total, so the purge removes 0% and costs nothing; with
   `inlineStylesheets: 'always'` (what Auburn runs) inline CSS goes from 2,052 KB to 1,015 KB, 51% removed, about
   128 KB to 63 KB a page. The step only pays on a site that inlines; it is harmless on one that does not.
2. **Headers** (`public/_headers`): a second `Content-Security-Policy: form-action 'self'` line (kept apart so card
   153's `/*` line stays byte-for-byte), `Permissions-Policy` refusing camera, microphone, geolocation, usb,
   magnetometer and gyroscope, and a day plus a week of `stale-while-revalidate` for `/og/*`, the favicons and the
   apple touch icon. `/_astro/*` already carried the immutable year. HSTS is unchanged (`includeSubDomains` stays).
   `docs/agent/deployment.md` says a pasted form that posts off-site needs its origin on `form-action`.
3. **`vite.build.assetsInlineLimit: 0`** in `astro.config.mjs`: small scripts ship as hashed `/_astro/` files, not
   inline, so the CSP hash list stays short. The starter's line is 652 bytes with 10 inline scripts. New
   `scripts/lib/headers-line-limit.test.mjs` (part of `test:unit`) pins the config and fails if a built or source
   `_headers` line passes 2,000 characters.
4. **No canonical on a noindex page** (`BaseLayout.astro`), with `tests/noindex-canonical.spec.ts`.
5. **JPEG share images:** `ogUrlFromImage` asks Sanity for `format('jpg').quality(80)` instead of `auto('format')`.

**Not ported.** Fonts and textures moved to `src/assets/`: the starter has none in `public/` (its fonts come from
`@fontsource` and are already hashed). Auburn's `og-card.mjs` change was only a font path, so the starter's
`render-og.mjs` (PORTABLE) is untouched; the JPEG change lives in BaseLayout. `svg-path-compact` (stone icons),
`print-icons.mjs`, the HSTS relaxation and the Toaster removal are Auburn-only: the starter's Toaster is still used
by `CopyEmailButton.tsx`. Auburn's `page-weight.spec.ts` is Auburn-specific.

**Applied:** starter (this card); first-baptist-auburn = source (applied). Other sites: copy the two PORTABLE files,
add the purge step to `build`, and apply the `_headers`, config and BaseLayout changes by hand. Gotcha note's
"Ported to" box for the starter can now be ticked once this merges.

## Card 160: Redirects from file-style addresses get an exact slashless rule (2026-10-25)

**Origin:** stonesteps-50k, 2026-10-25. Its #158 added Search Console redirects for `/index.htm` and
`/index_files/Registration.htm`; CI was green and both still 404ed live. Vault gotcha:
`trailing-slash-always-skips-redirects-from-file-paths`. **Canonical:** PORTABLE `src/lib/redirects.ts`
(`isFileStyleSource`, `fileStyleRedirectLines`, `prependRedirectLines`, + tests). Per site (NOT portable): the
`fileStyleRedirects()` integration in `astro.config.mjs` and its entry in `integrations`.

**Why.** With `trailingSlash: 'always'`, Astro writes every `redirects` source with a trailing slash, so
`'/index.htm': '/'` reaches `_redirects` as `/index.htm/ / 301`. Cloudflare adds a trailing slash itself only to an
extensionless path, so `/index.htm` never meets the rule and the asset layer answers 404. An extensionless source
(`/the-course`) still works, in two hops. The live 404 even showed `CF-Cache-Status: HIT`, which reads like a stale
deploy and is not: it is the cached 404 asset. Proved with `wrangler dev` on the built site before and after.

**What it does.** After the build, `fileStyleRedirects()` reads the final `redirects` map (launch entries and editor
entries alike, so a Studio redirect from an old `.html` or `.php` page is covered too), writes one exact, slashless
line per file-style source (`/index.htm / 301`) at the top of `dist/client/_redirects`, and skips any source a
hand-written `public/_redirects` already lists. The adapter appends its own rules to the same file in the same
hook; the result is the same whichever runs first. Dynamic sources (`/[slug].htm`) are skipped.

**Adapt per site:** copy the three functions (and tests) into `src/lib/redirects.ts`, add the integration block and
`fileStyleRedirects()` to `integrations`. A site that already carries exact rules by hand in `public/_redirects`
(stonesteps-50k#163) can keep them; the build step will not duplicate them. Check: build, then
`grep -n '\.htm\|\.php' dist/client/_redirects`, and curl the slashless form on `wrangler dev` or live.

**Applied (2026-10-25):** the build step and tests in first-baptist-auburn#189, fbcm#115, presacademy#134,
reid-design-site#181 and stonesteps-50k#164 (which keeps its hand-written rules; the step skips them, though
its log line counts them as "added"). Earlier: starter (this card). stonesteps-50k = source, `partial`: exact hand-written rules in
`public/_redirects` (#163), not the build step. No other family repo has a file-style redirect source today
(checked each `origin/main`, 2026-10-25), so the others are `no` until a client files one.

## Card 161: `snapshot.mjs run` reads the project id from the snapshot (2026-10-25)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn. Its CI `site` job built 19 pages where a local snapshot build of the same
snapshot built 28, and Plan your visit lost its Church and FAQPage JSON-LD. The job had no `PUBLIC_SANITY_*`
env. `sanityFetch` (src/lib/sanity.ts) treats a missing project id as "no Sanity" and returns its fallback
without a request, so `SANITY_SNAPSHOT_URL` was set and the snapshot server was never asked anything. Nothing
failed: every check passed against a site built from fallbacks.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE `scripts/snapshot.mjs` (+ `scripts/lib/snapshot.test.mjs`).

**What it does.** `run` merges .env into the env (`loadEnv`) and, when there is still no
`PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID`, takes the project and dataset from the snapshot's own asset URLs
(`cdn.sanity.io/images/<project>/<dataset>/...`, pure helper `snapshotProjectEnv`), so image URLs come out
right too, and logs `snapshot: project <id>/<dataset> (read from the snapshot)`. With no id anywhere and no asset
in the snapshot it stops with an error rather than build a site from fallbacks. A set id is never overridden.
The template path (no snapshot file, no project id) is unchanged.

**Per site (not portable):** set `PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID` / `PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET` at the workflow level in
`ci.yml` and `lighthouse.yml` anyway (fbcm and stonesteps-50k already do), so every job agrees.

## Card 165: the search index waits for Pagefind to finish writing (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn#204. Its CI artifact carried `pagefind/pagefind.js` cut at exactly 32,768 of 45,555
bytes, so every search said "Search is not available right now" and the search spec failed twice on the same
artifact. A local build of the same commit was whole. `build-search-index.mjs` (card 154) called
`pagefind.close()` straight after `writeFiles()`, which can resolve before Pagefind's binary has flushed every file,
and close() stops the binary. A deploy builds the same way, so live search could have shipped broken.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE `scripts/build-search-index.mjs`, `scripts/lib/search-files.mjs` (+ `search-files.test.mjs`).

**What it does.** After `writeFiles()` the build waits until `pagefind/` has stopped changing for half a second
(`waitForStableDir`, at most 15 s), then closes Pagefind, then syntax-checks every `.js` Pagefind wrote
(`brokenScripts`: `node --check` on a `.mjs` copy; a truncated file is a syntax error). If one is cut short the
build fails with `[search] pagefind/<file> is not valid JavaScript (cut short?)`, so CI and the deploy stop
instead of shipping a site whose search cannot start.

**Verified (2026-10-26):** `search-files.test.mjs` (a whole module passes, a cut one is caught; the wait returns
once a writer stops); `npm run test:scripts` 172 pass in first-baptist-auburn; the index step on Auburn's real
build writes the whole 45,555-byte `pagefind.js`.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin, with #204.

**Who should take it.** Any site with `search.enabled` (today only first-baptist-auburn).

## Card 171: Short links written into `_redirects` at build time, and a QR code action in the Studio (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn #212. The church wanted `/vbs`-style addresses for bulletins and QR codes without
asking a developer each season, and printable codes that keep working when a page is renamed.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE `src/lib/short-links.ts` (address shape, clash rules, expiry, the `_redirects` lines) and
`src/lib/short-links.test.ts`; PORTABLE `src/lib/qr.ts` (SVG path, PNG scale, file name) and `src/lib/qr.test.ts`
(against the real library); PORTABLE `src/sanity/actions/qrCode.tsx` (the "QR code" document action) and
`src/sanity/components/ShortLinkAddressInput.tsx` (the live "People type example.com/spring" line). Already-PORTABLE
`src/lib/studio-icons.ts` gains `shortLink: 'link'` in the type icon defaults. Per site, not marked:
`src/sanity/schemaTypes/shortLink.ts` (wording, `PAGE_TARGETS` with scaffold markers, `LAUNCH_FORWARDS`),
`src/sanity/guides/links.ts` (two Site Guide entries), the Quick update tile in `kit.config.ts`, the
`shortLinks()` integration in `astro.config.mjs`, `site.timeZone` in `src/data/site.ts`. New dependency
`qrcode-generator` 2.0.4 (MIT, no dependencies), imported lazily by the action only, so it never reaches a public
page. Docs: `docs/agent/seo.md`, "Short links" and "QR codes".

**What it does.** Pages > Short links (or Quick update, "Make a short link") makes a `shortLink`: a short address,
a page reference (follows a rename) or an outside URL, "For now" (302, the default) or "For good" (301), and an
optional last day. The `shortLinks()` integration reads the published ones at build time and writes `/x` and `/x/`
at the TOP of `dist/client/_redirects`, after card 160's `fileStyleRedirects()`, so either form is one hop. It
skips, and logs, an expired link (the day after its last day, in `site.timeZone`), a clash with a reserved slug
(`src/lib/reservedSlugs.ts`), a published page, any key of the config's `redirects` map (editor redirects, launch
redirects and card 160's file-style sources alike), or an older short link; pages always win. It caps short links at
200 (400 lines) and fails the build only if the whole file would pass Cloudflare's 2,000 static rules. The Studio
shows the same clashes as errors on the address field before publishing (an archived page as a warning). Every short
link and every document with a page of its own gets "QR code" in its document menu: SVG for print, PNG for Word or
slides, a short link's code holding the short address and a page's its full address on `site.url`; while
`site.domain` is a `workers.dev` address the dialog warns the codes point at the temporary address. Private pages
and the not-found page get no button.

**Switching it on.** Nothing to switch: with no short links the integration writes nothing, and with no Sanity
project `cmsQuery` returns the empty fallback. Set `site.timeZone` to the client's IANA zone (the starter's default is `'America/New_York'`, set by card 173).
A site that wants an expired link to stop "the next morning" adds a daily `schedule` to `deploy.yml`; otherwise it
stops at the next publish or push. A site with hand-written launch redirects lists their old addresses in
`LAUNCH_FORWARDS` in `shortLink.ts` so the Studio warns too (the build reads the real map regardless). A site with
more routed types adds them to `PAGE_TARGETS` and `pathForDoc()`.

**Not ported:** Auburn's church wording (bulletins, "the church's own address") and its daily 10:00 UTC rebuild
(a deploy schedule is a per-site choice). `todayIn` no longer defaults to New York: the caller passes the zone
(Auburn passes its `CHURCH_TIME_ZONE`). The example words in the address messages are now "spring" and "signup".

**Verified (2026-10-26):** in the starter, `npm run check`, `npm run build` (no Sanity project: no short links, no
change to `_redirects`), `npm run test:unit` (short-links and qr tests included). first-baptist-auburn on its
snapshot build: the same gates, `sync-check` against this branch all SAME. The signed-in Studio dialog was not
clicked through in this card (Auburn's #212 verified it).

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin; its copies of the four marked files (and
`studio-icons.ts`) become the starter's, and its `astro.config.mjs` passes `CHURCH_TIME_ZONE` to `todayIn`.

**Who should take it.** Any site whose editors print flyers or want campaign addresses: presacademy, mas-monograms,
stonesteps-50k, reid-design-site, nixoncreativestudio. Copy the marked files, the schema, guides, tile, integration

## Card 168: Logo and square icon uploads in Site settings, the icon becomes the favicon set (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn (#212, the Studio self-serve work). The pastor asked how he would change the logo
or the tab icon without a developer. The starter already had an optional `logo` upload with no guard rails (a 120 px
PNG went in and looked blurry in the header), and no way at all to change the favicon set without `npm run favicon`
and a commit.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE `scripts/build-brand-icons.mjs` (the post-build step), `scripts/lib/brand-icons.mjs` (the
drawing: ICO, the SVG wrapper, every PNG size, the maskable plate, the cached download, and `iconDataUri` for a site
that puts the mark on its share cards) and `scripts/lib/brand-icons.test.mjs`, `scripts/lib/build-sanity-client.mjs`
(the read-only client post-build steps share: published content, the CI snapshot when set, null with no project
id), `src/lib/brand-uploads.ts` and `src/lib/brand-uploads.test.ts` (the size rules). Site files:
`src/sanity/components/BrandImageInput.tsx` (the preview under each field), the `logo` and `siteIcon` fields in
`src/sanity/schemaTypes/siteSettings.ts`, the guide "Change the logo or the icon". Docs: `docs/agent/sanity.md`,
"Logo and icon from the Studio".

**What it does.**

- **Logo** (the existing field): SVG best; a raster under 400 px wide is refused, under 560 px or squarish (narrower
  than 1.5 to 1) gets a warning. The size comes from the asset id (`image-<hash>-<w>x<h>-<ext>`), so the check runs
  the moment a file is chosen, with no extra request.
- **Square icon** (`siteIcon`, new, optional): must be square (2% slack) and, for a raster, at least 512 px. At build
  time `build-brand-icons.mjs` (in `npm run build`, after the CSS purge) writes favicon.ico (16/32/48),
  favicon.svg (the SVG itself, or the PNG wrapped in one), apple-touch-icon, icon-192, icon-512 and
  icon-maskable-512 into `dist/client` over the committed copies. The names do not change, so BaseLayout's links,
  `site.webmanifest`, the Studio's corner mark and the Studio app manifest follow with no edit. The plate behind the
  home-screen and maskable icons is the manifest's `background_color`.
- **A preview** under each field: the logo in the header in light and dark, the icon in a browser tab and on a home
  screen (round crop too); the template's own files while empty.
- **Never a red build.** No project id, nothing uploaded, Sanity unreachable, or a file sharp cannot read: one log
  line and the committed icons ship. The download is cached by URL in `node_modules/.cache/brand-icon` (Sanity asset
  URLs are content hashes).

**Switching it on.** Nothing: both fields are empty by default and the committed icons keep shipping. An editor
uploads, publishes, and the publish webhook's rebuild carries it.

**Not ported:** Auburn's other uses of `siteIcon` (its footer mark, Home's small mark, the podcast artwork) and its
preview's footer tile, because they draw Auburn's own chrome; a site that wants them reads `siteIcon` in its own
query. Auburn's field wording ("the brand kit's files are the recommended ones") stays in its schema. The share-card
mark is card 169.

**Verified (2026-10-26):** `npm run check`, `npm run test:unit` (new `brand-icons.test.mjs` draws the set from an SVG
and a PNG and checks every size; `brand-uploads.test.ts`) and `npm run build` with no project (prints the "no icon"
line, the committed icons ship) in the starter. first-baptist-auburn's branch: `sync-check` against this starter all
SAME, `npm run check`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run build` against its dataset. That build found a bug the origin
had: on Windows, `process.exit(0)` after the Sanity read tripped a libuv assertion ("UV_HANDLE_CLOSING", exit 127)
and failed `npm run build`; the script now ends without calling exit. Not verified: the preview under the fields in
a signed-in Studio (the starter worktree has no project).

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin (its copies now match the starter's byte for byte; the
logo warning says "a mark with the name beside it" instead of "the cross with the name beside it").

**Who should take it.** Every site whose owner might change their logo or icon: copy the five PORTABLE files and the
test, add `node scripts/build-brand-icons.mjs` to `npm run build` after `astro build`, add the two fields (or the
validation and input on an existing `logo`) and a site version of `BrandImageInput.tsx`, run typegen.

## Card 169: Share cards make themselves at build time (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn (#212). Per-page share cards were committed PNGs drawn by hand with
`npm run og:pages`, so a renamed page or a new post shared a stale card or none: the starter's BaseLayout pointed
og:image at `/og/<route>.png` whether or not the file existed. The starter's own `public/og/` still held 23 cards
from the client build it was forked from.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE `scripts/build-og-cards.mjs` (the post-build step), `scripts/lib/og-build.mjs` and
`og-build.test.mjs` (the marker, the HTML rewrites, the fallback), `src/lib/og-card-marker.ts` and its test (which
share image a page uses, and the marker). Changed PORTABLE files: `scripts/lib/render-og.mjs` (new `ogCardHtml` and
`renderOgHtml` exports, an optional kicker and mark, and a Chrome or Edge fallback when Playwright's Chromium is not
installed; og-default.png's HTML is byte-identical without them) and `src/sanity/schemaTypes/_seoFields.ts` (the
Social share image description no longer says "Leave blank to use the site default"). Site files:
`scripts/lib/og-card.mjs` (the card design: `cardHtml`, `renderHtml`, `closeCards`), BaseLayout's `ogCard` prop,
the `siteSettings.seoImage` description. Uses `scripts/lib/build-sanity-client.mjs` and `brand-icons.mjs` from card 168. Docs: `docs/agent/seo.md`, "Share images make themselves".

**What it does.**

- BaseLayout resolves the share image in this order: a picture the page passes (a post's cover), the page's own
  Share image, **the generated card** at `/og/<route>.jpg` (every prerendered page), Site settings' default (now
  only for pages rendered on request, the password pages), `og-default.png`. For the card it writes an
  `x-og-card` marker (base64url JSON: title, kicker, home). Pages pass `ogCard`: Home `{ home: true }` (the site
  name with the tagline), journal posts their date, the journal index its eyebrow.
- `build-og-cards.mjs` (in `npm run build` after the icon step) draws each marked page's card as a JPEG into
  `dist/client/og/`, adds `?v=<hash>` to og:image so Facebook and text apps refetch a changed card, and removes the
  marker. Site settings' square icon (card 168), when uploaded, goes on every card as `mark`.
- **Fast:** each card is cached by a hash of its full HTML in `node_modules/.cache/og-cards`, kept between CI,
  Lighthouse and deploy runs by `actions/cache`; a warm build draws nothing.
- **Never a red build:** Playwright's Chromium, else the machine's Chrome or Edge (a GitHub runner's Chrome); with no
  browser, or a card that fails, those pages share `og-default.png` with a warning. No Sanity project still draws
  every card (the starter's own build does), only the Studio icon is skipped.
- Retired: `scripts/generate-og-pages.mjs`, `npm run og:pages`, apply-brand's rewrite of it, and the committed
  `public/og/*.png`. `npm run og` still draws the committed `og-default.png`. deploy.yml's "add a freshness
  check here" note is replaced: a card cannot go stale.

**Switching it on.** Nothing: it runs in every build. A site with its own card design replaces
`scripts/lib/og-card.mjs` and keeps the three exports.

**Not ported:** Auburn's card design ("night": the navy tile ground, brick sill, building sketch, the title fitted
from 108px down to 60px), which stays in its own `og-card.mjs`; the starter's card is the generic one from
`render-og.mjs` in `og-theme.mjs`'s colors. Auburn's per-page kickers (sermons, series, bulletin) stay in its pages.

**Verified (2026-10-26):** in the starter, `npm run check`, `npm run test:unit` (`og-build.test.mjs`,
`og-card-marker.test.ts`) and `npm run build` with no project: "Share cards: 16 pages, 16 drawn" in 1.6 s, og:image
reads `/og/home.jpg?v=<hash>` and no page keeps the marker; the generic card checked by eye (page card with a
kicker, Home card). first-baptist-auburn's branch: `sync-check` all SAME (348), `npm run check`, `npm run test:unit`,
`npm run build` against its dataset (29 night cards through the PORTABLE step). The no-browser fallback is the
origin's code, unchanged; not re-run here.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin (its copies now match the starter's byte for byte).

## Card 172: Embed provider registry, paste-and-go and a per-build embed CSP (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn #212 (2026-10-26). Editors pasted YouTube watch links, Maps share links and giving
widgets into the Custom code or embed block (card 121) and got blank frames, wrong shapes, or a widget that only worked
with "Runs directly on the page" on, which let any pasted script run with the site's own trust.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE `src/lib/embed-providers.ts` (the registry and every decision) and its test
`src/lib/embed-providers.test.ts`; PORTABLE `src/sanity/components/EmbedPasteInput.tsx` (`makeEmbedPasteInput()`);
PORTABLE `tests/embed-guard.spec.ts`. Already-PORTABLE files changed: `scripts/build-csp.mjs` (reads the embed
markers), `scripts/lib/csp.mjs` (`embedProviderIds()`) and `scripts/lib/csp.test.mjs`. Site files changed (not
marked): `src/components/sections/EmbedSection.astro`, `src/components/SectionRenderer.astro` (`trustedCode`),
`src/sanity/schemaTypes/sections.ts` (`EMBED_WORDS`, validations, hidden Height), `src/pages/styleguide/sections.astro`
(`GUARD_CHECKS`), `src/data/site.ts` (`embeds.approvedScriptOrigins`), `package.json` (`build`). Docs:
`docs/agent/custom-code.md` ("Paste-and-go"), `docs/agent/deployment.md` ("Security headers"),
`docs/claude/build-and-scripts.md`, `docs/claude/topic-index.md`.

**What it does.**

- One paste box on the block. A link, or code that is only an iframe, goes into `embedUrl`; other code into
  `embedCode`, with "Runs directly on the page" switched on only when every script is a known service's. Nothing new is
  stored: the plan is worked out again in the Studio and on every build (rule 15).
- Fifteen services: YouTube, Vimeo, Facebook video, Google Maps, Calendar and Forms, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Calendly,
  and the church family's Church Trac, Planning Center, Tithe.ly, Givelify, Subsplash, SignUpGenius. Share links become
  embeddable ones (YouTube to `youtube-nocookie.com/embed`, Spotify to its player, a Calendar `?cid=` to `embed?src=`)
  at the right shape (16:9 or a fixed height), and the Height choice hides. A link that cannot be framed (a Maps share
  link, a Facebook page, a Form's edit link) is a field error saying what to paste instead.
- The guard rail: script code from a service the registry does not know never runs on the page, even with the switch
  on; it stays in its sandboxed box and the Studio says who must approve it. Approve for every site with a registry
  entry here; for one site's one-off widget, add its origin to `site.embeds.approvedScriptOrigins`. Repo-written
  styleguide probes pass `trustedCode` (never Sanity content).
- CSP: code from a known service carries `data-embed-provider="<id>"`; `build-csp.mjs` looks each id up in the registry
  and adds that service's script hosts and their subdomains to `script-src`, only on a build where a page uses it.

**Why the CSP folds into `build-csp.mjs`.** Auburn shipped it as a second script (`build-embed-csp.mjs` plus
`scripts/lib/embed-csp.mjs`) that re-opened the `_headers` line and spliced origins in, because the registry was
Auburn's and `build-csp.mjs` was PORTABLE. With the registry PORTABLE too, the fold is about ten lines: the origins go
into the same `extra` list as GA4 and `csp-origins.json`, so there is one writer, one 2,000-character check, and no
second parser of the policy line. The registry is TypeScript, so `build-csp.mjs` imports it only when a page carries a
marker and the file exists (a site without card 172 never touches it), and `package.json` runs it with
`--experimental-strip-types` (needed on Node 22.12 to 22.17, harmless later). Only registry ids count, so a marker
typed into pasted code names no origin of its own.

**Switching it on.** Nothing to set: it is on for every page-builder site that takes the files. Per site: set
`EMBED_WORDS` in `sections.ts` (who approves, which examples the empty block names). No env, no secret.

**Not ported:** none of the logic; Auburn's Studio wording stays in Auburn's `sections.ts`. The church services stay
in the generic registry because they cost a site that never pastes them nothing. Their script hosts (Givelify,
Subsplash, SignUpGenius especially) are each service's main domain, NOT verified against real snippets: if one loads
from elsewhere the Studio says "not known", and the fix is a registry line here.

**Verified (2026-10-26):** starter `npm run check`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run build`, and
`tests/embed-guard.spec.ts` plus `tests/custom-code.spec.ts` (6 passed); the guard fixtures screenshotted at 375 and
1280 in light and dark, no horizontal scroll. `build-csp.mjs` run over a page carrying a `tithely` marker and a bogus
one: `script-src` gains the four Tithe.ly origins, the bogus id adds nothing, and with no registry file present nothing
is imported. first-baptist-auburn branch: the same gates green, sync-check 341 SAME against this branch. The Studio
paste box itself was not exercised signed in.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin (its branch `port/card-172` swaps to the PORTABLE copies
and deletes `build-embed-csp.mjs` and `scripts/lib/embed-csp.mjs`).

**Who should take it.** Every page-builder site with the Custom code or embed block (card 121): presacademy,
reid-design-site, mas-monograms, nixoncreativestudio, stonesteps-50k. Take all the marked files together:
`build-csp.mjs` without `embed-providers.ts` is safe (it imports only on a marker), but `EmbedSection.astro` needs both.

## Card 173: the builder kit: twelve smaller blocks, grouped templates, patterns as code (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn, 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-26 (its church section library, the letter block and PR #217,
the event and holiday page blocks). The card 109 kit let an editor start from a template and reuse sections, but the
block library was still the big pieces only: a hero, text, a photo beside text, a gallery. An editor who wanted a
closure notice, a countdown, two columns of text, a row of buttons, an event page with "Add to my calendar", or a
note from the owner had to ask a developer. Auburn built those for a pastor editing alone; this card is their generic
half. **Canonical:** the starter. No file is marked PORTABLE: every piece touches files each site has adapted
(`sections.ts`, `queries.ts`, `SectionRenderer.astro`, `pageBuilder.types.ts`), and templates and patterns are per
site by design.

**What it is.**

- **Twelve blocks** in `src/sanity/schemaTypes/builderSections.ts`, spread into `pageSectionSchemas`: text in columns,
  a row of buttons or link cards, one wide photo (photo viewer, card 124), fold-out questions (native `<details>`),
  tabs (WAI-ARIA keyboard pattern, every panel readable without JavaScript), a countdown, a dated notice, a timeline,
  a letter, event details, a schedule and cards with photos. Components in `src/components/builder-blocks/`
  (`BuilderBlock.astro` picks one; `SectionRenderer` has a single `isBuilderBlock()` branch), styles in
  `src/styles/builder-blocks.css` (theme tokens only, so light, dark and the Feature band need nothing extra), types in
  `src/lib/builderBlocks.types.ts`, projection arms in `SECTION_ARMS`.
- **Rule 15 logic** in `src/lib/builder-blocks.ts` (pinned by `builder-blocks.test.ts`): whether a notice is in its
  window, the countdown's phase and days, quarter-hour time options, which event dates are still to come, the
  `.ics` (through card 158's `buildIcs`, handed over as a `data:` link so no route or file is published), the
  directions link, one schema.org `Event` per date with the zone's offset for that day, and the card column count.
  Dates are calendar days in the new `site.timeZone` (`src/data/site.ts`), which the RSVP emails now read too. The
  notice and countdown recount in the browser, so a page built yesterday is still right today.
- **Generic where Auburn was the church's:** event details takes a REQUIRED typed place (Auburn falls back to the
  church address in Church facts, which the starter does not have); the letter is "a note from" any role; the notice
  links any ten-digit phone number; no brick or stone art, the shapes are the starter's cards, hairlines and radius.
- **Rules kept:** no colour field (rule 9; `builderSections` is now in the section-fields gate's libraries); every
  block but the notice is a content block with a `look` (the photo and the letter offer Standard and Quiet only); the
  notice is self-contained; `urgency`, `startTime` and `endTime` are in `NON_STEGA_FIELDS` (rule 8b); the
  notice's urgency and the preset countdown and letter lines are setting keys, so an untouched block still reads as
  empty; the event's main button can be the page's one accent button (card 158).
- **Grouped templates.** `PageTemplate.group`, `TEMPLATE_GROUPS` and `templateMenuTitle()` show each template as
  "Group: Title" in the new-document menu (it has no headings). The starter's set: Basics (Simple page, Landing page,
  Questions page, Blank page), About (About us, Meet the team), Events (Event page: event details, schedule, photo
  cards, fold-outs), Announcements (Notice page). Written with the builders in `src/sanity/templateBlocks.ts`
  (`example()` markers; `daysFromNow()` so a new event page opens with dates still to come).
- **Patterns as code.** `src/sanity/sectionPatterns.ts` (closure notice, event details with a schedule, common
  questions) and `npm run seed:patterns` (`scripts/seed-section-patterns.mjs`): one DRAFT `sectionPreset` per
  pattern, id `pattern-<id>`, any existing draft or published id skipped, dry by default, production behind
  `--apply` and `NCS_PRODUCTION_WRITE=yes` (card 86). Drafts so example text can never go live through a synced
  section.
- **`withSiteGroups()`** (`src/lib/insert-groups.ts`, tested; Auburn's `withChurchGroups`): merges a library's insert
  groups into the base menu by name. The kit adds Basics entries and two groups, "Events and notices" and "Fold-outs
  and tabs". A fork adds its own library's groups to `SITE_INSERT_GROUPS` in `sections.ts` and never edits the base

**Tests.** `builder-blocks.test.ts`, `insert-groups.test.ts`; `authoring.test.ts` now checks templates AND patterns
for group order, known block types, fresh keys, the example marker, copy rules (no em-dashes, AI-tell words, UK

fold-outs, the event's calendar link, directions and JSON-LD, the countdown and the notice. Every block has a fixture

**Skipped from Auburn, and why.** The church-only blocks (service times, map, scripture, beliefs, giving, sermons,

**Adopting it in a site.** Copy `builderSections.ts`, `src/components/builder-blocks/`, `builder-blocks.css`,

## Card 177: Calendar files can skip or move one date of a repeating event (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn's "A different Sunday" (its PR #212): when a weekly gathering is cancelled or meets
at another time one week, its `.ics` files say so. Auburn first spliced EXDATE and RECURRENCE-ID lines into
`buildIcs`'s finished string in `src/lib/gatherings.ts`; the exception fields now live in `buildIcs` itself.

**Canonical:** PORTABLE `src/lib/ics.ts` (already PORTABLE since card 158; this card changes it) and
`src/lib/ics.test.ts`. Docs: `docs/agent/components.md` ("Calendar files").

**What it does.** `IcsEvent` gains two optional fields. `exdate: IcsTime[]` writes one `EXDATE` line per date
straight after the `RRULE` (RFC 5545 3.8.5.1): the occurrence the series would have had, so calendar apps drop it.
`recurrenceId: IcsTime` makes the event an override (3.8.4.4): same `uid` as the series, `RECURRENCE-ID` is the
occurrence's ORIGINAL date-time (written just before `DTSTART`), and `start` is its new one, so the app moves that
one date and keeps the series. `buildIcs` throws on what the RFC forbids: an exception written differently from
`start` (UTC, all-day or another zone), an `exdate` with no `rrule`, an override with an `rrule` or `exdate`.
An event without the new fields is written byte for byte as before, so existing routes do not change.

**Switching it on:** nothing; pass the fields when a site has a cancelled or moved date. The header comment of
`ics.ts` has a worked weekly example.

**Not ported:** "A different Sunday" itself (the `timeChanges` list in Site settings, `dayPlan()` and
`gatheringExceptions()` in `src/lib/church-facts.ts`, its Studio panel and the banner and This Sunday wording)
stays in first-baptist-auburn, because it is built on the church's facts model (service times keyed by gathering,
the `confirmed` flags, the Church Trac feed), which the starter does not have. Auburn's `/sunday.ics` is still
hand-written in `church-facts.ts` (it predates `buildIcs`); moving it onto `buildIcs` is Auburn's own follow-up.

**Verified (2026-10-26):** `node --test src/lib/ics.test.ts` (11 tests: EXDATE in a zone, all-day `VALUE=DATE`
and UTC forms, the override's UID, `RECURRENCE-ID` and `DTSTART` order with no `RRULE`, one VTIMEZONE, the
unchanged no-exception output, and every throw), `npm run check`, `npm run test:unit` and `npm run build` in the
starter. In first-baptist-auburn, `gatheringIcs()` now passes `exdate` and an override event instead of
splicing; its `sunday-changes` and `gatherings` unit tests pass unchanged and `sync-check` reports SAME.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin.

**Who should take it.** Any site that writes `.ics` files for repeating events (today only first-baptist-auburn).
Sites that do not use `ics.ts` take the copy with the next sync and see no change.

## Card 178: An optional button left empty no longer blocks Publish (2026-10-26)

**Origin:** first-baptist-auburn, building a Christmas page in the live Studio (its PR #224): a fresh Event details block
stopped Publish with "Button text: Required" and "Link type: Required" on its OPTIONAL button.

**Cause.** `ctaBlock`'s `openInNewTab` had `initialValue: false`. Sanity fills initial values when an object is created, so
every new block with an optional `type: 'ctaBlock'` field got a half-made button object, and the button's `label` and
`linkType` (both `Rule.required()`) then fired although the editor never touched the button.

**Fix.** Three files, none PORTABLE.

- `src/sanity/schemaTypes/ctaBlock.ts`: an `inUse(parent)` helper (any of label, linkType, internalLink, externalUrl,
  emailAddress, phoneNumber set). `label` and `linkType` are required only when the button is in use, with plain messages;
  `openInNewTab` has no `initialValue`.
- `src/components/CtaLink.astro`: a cta OBJECT with no label, no linkType and no href renders nothing. `cta` undefined
  still takes the fallbacks.
- `src/components/SectionRenderer.astro`: a closing band whose cta object is empty no longer counts toward the page's one
  accent button (`primaryBudget`), since it draws nothing.

**Checked before changing render:** every `ctaBandSection` in `scripts/seed-core.mjs` and the styleguide fixtures carries a
label, so none relied on an empty object drawing the fallback.

**Differs from Auburn:** the starter has no `drawsRed` helper; the budget lives in the `primaryBudget` callback.

**Applied:** starter (this card). first-baptist-auburn: origin. Not applied to the other family sites: **every site that uses
`ctaBlock` has the bug** (any optional button field). Port the three files and check that no page relied on an empty
button drawing "Get in touch".
